  decision contract            —   [canon: DC 6-tuple]
  admissibility conjunction over exactly those 6 —   [MISSING — registered]
  authority → gate binding     —   [MISSING]
  authority-act object         —   [NOT ESTABLISHED in canon]
  ...
  ⚠ policy-loop termination    —   [OPEN: two unreconciled resolutions stand — GC-1]
b_rows_sample.statement: The Governance/Authority Model template section (6.8) is rated PARTIAL with an open collision: canon fixes authority-as-a-precondition-constraint, authority-not-equal-to-evidential-truth (I-4), the Accepted->Committed boundary-crossing act (A6), and the Decision Contract 6-tuple shape, but has no admissibility conjunction over exactly those six fields, no authority-to-gate binding, no typed authority-act object, and the GC-1 policy-loop termination remains open with two unreconciled resolutions standing.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
> **The ratified canon defines when a transition would be ILLEGAL without ever defining what a
> transition IS.**

Two legality constraints are ratified — **I-12** ... and **A6** ... Both constrain a transition relation that the canon never specifies.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central finding: the ratified canon defines two legality CONSTRAINTS on state transitions (I-12, the ladder's covering relation excluding skipped moves; A6, that only an authority act, never evidence volume, crosses the Accepted->Committed boundary) without ever defining what a transition itself IS (no signature, no legality condition, no pre/post-conditions); a law quantifying over an undefined relation is not executable, so 'legal transition rules' reach 'ratified' status only as constraints, never as executable semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **Postconditions** | **not even mentioned** | Zero occurrences of `postcondition` / `post-condition` anywhere in `model/` or `final-architecture/`. |
b_rows_sample.statement: A textual search finds zero occurrences of the strings 'postcondition' or 'post-condition' anywhere in the model/ or final-architecture/ directories of the ratified corpus, while 'precondition' occurs exactly once, describing Authorization's conceptual role (COMPOSITION grade) rather than serving as any specific operation's precondition; preservation obligations and rejection/invalid-transition semantics are both found NOT ESTABLISHED (no artifact maps any operation to invariants it must preserve, and no typed rejection vocabulary -- structural vs policy vs authority refusal -- exists despite the Decision Contract 6-tuple implicitly needing one).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
## D · Status declaration

```
Transformations = BLOCKED / NOT CANONICAL
Blocked behind:  the operation registry (primary)
                 state identity + equality (secondary)
                 a closed invariant register (secondary)
```
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally declares Transformations = BLOCKED/NOT CANONICAL, and identifies three specific dependency reasons this cannot be filled in isolation: (1) primary -- a transformation contract is written per-operation, and with zero ratified operations there is nothing to write contracts for, so Transformations is blocked BEHIND Operations, not merely alongside it; (2) secondary -- a postcondition is a predicate over the resulting state, which cannot be checked until K1=K2 is decidable, and canon defines neither identity nor equality; (3) secondary -- 'preserves invariant I-n' presupposes the set of I-n is closed, but canon asserts twelve invariants without asserting that is all of them.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
## A · Capabilities the ratified canon REQUIRES but does not define

... | C-1 | move an item one rung up the ladder | ladder + **I-12** | **NO** | yes — layer 2, unratified |
...
**Nine capabilities are canonically required. Zero operations are canonically defined.** That
sentence is the whole gap.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies nine capabilities (C-1..C-9) that the ratified canon logically requires to exist, each traced to a specific ratified forcing element, for none of which is an actual operation defined: C-1 move a ladder rung up (I-12); C-2 attach Committed to an Accepted item by authority act (A6, I-4); C-3 make a Determination Supported->Accepted under AcceptancePolicy (v0.1 concept row, grade READ); C-4 change an in-force policy version via governed decision (I-11, R-1 stratification loop -- GC-1 open); C-5 compose evidence so duplicates don't amplify and corroboration does (I-5, I-6, aggregation operator open by ruling OQ-3); C-6 compute the gap between state and requirement (Zero(K,EC), EC=eta(G,IdealState), R-2); C-7 turn an observation into evidence (the qualification predicate, undefined in canon); C-8 evaluate a decision contract for admissibility (DC 6-tuple, no ratified conjunction over exactly those six); C-9 act and observe the result (the decision interlock, far side open by ruling OQ-4). For every one of the nine, an unratified layer-2 candidate exists outside canon, but none is defined as canon.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
**Reading:** the canon fixes *fragments* — a precondition here, an authority requirement there —
around operations it never defines. Eleven properties × nine capabilities = 99 cells; **9 are
partially fixed by canon, 2 are fully fixed (C-2's authority requirement and its evidence
non-effect), and 88 are empty.** No capability has a complete contract. Not one.
b_rows_sample.statement: A systematic 11-required-property x 9-capability matrix (99 cells: Name, Purpose, Input state, Preconditions, Postconditions, Invariants preserved, Evidence generated/changed, Authority required, Replay semantics, Failure semantics, Ratification status) is filled from the ratified canon only: 9 cells are partially fixed (e.g. C-1/C-2/C-3/C-4 preconditions partially known via I-12/A6/I-11), exactly 2 cells are fully fixed (C-2's authority requirement being YES via A6/I-4, and its evidence-generated field being definitively NONE since evidence cannot cross the boundary per A6), and 88 of 99 cells are entirely empty; the reading is that canon fixes only fragments around operations it never actually defines, so no capability among the nine has a complete contract.

type_signature.domain: 11 required operation properties x 9 required capabilities

b_rows_sample.anchor:
## C · What must be decided (not answered here)

1. **Membership** ... 2. **Granularity** ... 3. **Per-operation contracts** ... 4. **Typed failure semantics** ... 5. **The C-2 asymmetry** — canon already fixes that authority crosses the boundary and evidence
   does not. Any operation definition must preserve that, and it is a ratified constraint on the
   answer, not part of the question.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists five things that must still be decided (not answered by this analysis itself): (1) membership -- which capabilities become operations and whether the resulting set is closed, given three non-agreeing candidate lists in layer 2 with an unexecuted minimality test; (2) granularity -- whether C-1..C-9 map one-to-one onto operations, noting layer-2 work already records operations do not map one-to-one onto state fields; (3) full per-operation contracts across the eleven properties; (4) a typed vocabulary for rejection/failure semantics; (5) the C-2 authority/evidence asymmetry (authority crosses the boundary, evidence never does, per A6/I-4) is stated to be a ratified CONSTRAINT that any future operation definition must satisfy, not an open part of the question itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Decision-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the causal link between epistemic states and the decisions they inform. When a knowledge state changes, its associated decisions SHALL be flagged for re-evaluation, ensuring that actions do not outlive their justification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap 1 (Decision Coupling, Knowledge->Action): identifies a missing invariant coupling knowledge states to the decisions/actions they justify, so that a stale/invalidated knowledge state flags dependent decisions for re-evaluation; proposed as H-KOS-Decision-001; without it, truth-seeking is 'useless for engineering or governance'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Revisability-001: No knowledge state SHALL be irrevocably finalized. The kernel MUST provide a governed path for revision (retraction, replacement, or refinement) for every knowledge object, preserving the revision history as part of its identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap 2 (Revisability as a Constitutional Right / Fallibilism): truth-seeking requires all knowledge remain revisable, turning the earlier TMS/AGM revision research into a constitutional law; proposed as H-KOS-Revisability-001; without it, the system degenerates into a dogma-storage system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Inference-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL distinguish between observational knowledge (evidenced externally) and inferential knowledge (evidenced internally via logic). The provenance of inferential knowledge MUST include its entire reasoning chain, and its authority is dependent on the validity of that chain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap 3 (Inference vs. Observation boundary): base/observed knowledge (external evidence) and derived/inferred knowledge (internal reasoning-chain evidence) have different authority models and are currently treated uniformly as 'evidence'; proposed as H-KOS-Inference-001; without it, systems conflate 'I read this' with 'I logically deduced this' -- a catastrophic epistemic category error.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Justification-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the logical type (monotonic/non-monotonic) and justification strength (deductive, inductive, abductive, probabilistic) of the reasoning applied. This logical metadata SHALL govern how contradictions are resolved and how evidence is weighted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap 4 (Justification Strength/Type): distinguishes monotonic/deductive (binary valid/invalid) from non-monotonic/defeasible (probabilistic/provisional) justification; proposed as H-KOS-Justification-001; explicit caution against building a full 'logic taxonomy kernel' -- the invariant is to not hide the nature of justification, not to store every logic type.

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-Decision-001 (Candidate): KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the relationship between a knowledge state and decisions derived from it. Changes to supporting knowledge SHALL trigger epistemic re-evaluation of dependent decisions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 1: 'Very strong candidate'; the invariant is NOT 'knowledge controls action' but 'action must preserve the epistemic basis that justified it'; connects to EKS observation!=decision, PKS assessment!=authority, AIP recommendation!=execution (out-of-group); refined as INV-KOS-Decision-001, status Candidate, needs a P5 domain-independence test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The statement: > No knowledge state SHALL be irrevocably finalized. is slightly too strong. ... The better invariant: ## INV-KOS-Revisability-001 (Candidate): KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the possibility of epistemic revision while preserving historical identity and provenance of previous states.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 2: 'Extremely strong', close to a constitutional principle; corrects H-KOS-Revisability-001's 'no knowledge state SHALL be irrevocably finalized' as too strong (counterexample: terminal states like archived historical fact, final legal judgment, mathematical proof), refining to INV-KOS-Revisability-001, status Very strong candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Some domains have terminal states: Examples: historical fact after archival closure, legal judgment after final appeal, mathematical proof
a_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample used to soften the Revisability/Fallibilism hypothesis: some domains (archived historical fact, legal judgment after final appeal, mathematical proof) legitimately have terminal, non-revisable states.

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-Inference-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL distinguish observed facts from derived conclusions. Derived knowledge SHALL preserve the reasoning path and premises from which it was generated. Status: Very strong candidate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 3: 'probably one of the strongest additions', already implicit in existing Evidence!=Authority/Observation!=Decision/Assessment!=Authority/Projection!=Source separations; formalized as INV-KOS-Inference-001 (Observation != Inference), status Very strong candidate; the failure mode named is an AI 'model generated statement treated as observation'.

a_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 4: 'important, but needs caution' -- risk of accidentally building a 'logic taxonomy kernel'; the invariant is 'do not hide the nature of justification', not 'store all logic types'; formalized as INV-KOS-Justification-001, status Candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision coupling | Strong candidate ... Revisability | Very strong candidate ... Observation vs inference | Very strong candidate ... Justification type | Candidate. They do not yet prove a kernel design.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final classification table of the four new gap-candidates by strength (Decision coupling: Strong; Revisability: Very strong; Observation vs inference: Very strong; Justification type: Candidate); explicitly states they do not yet prove a kernel design, but transform KnowledgeOS's framing from 'a system that preserves knowledge' to 'a constitutional epistemic system that preserves the conditions under which reasoning can approach truth without corrupting itself'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every inference SHALL preserve validated relation strength between premise and conclusion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Savyabhicara (invalid generalization; Nyaya example 'Hill has fire because Hill is knowable') is mapped to an AI hallucination pattern: observing 'System uses Kubernetes' and over-inferring 'therefore it is cloud-native' (false, since Kubernetes can be on-premise/hybrid). Derived invariant H-KOS-Inference-Consistency-001: 'Every inference SHALL preserve validated relation strength between premise and conclusion.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: A justification SHALL NOT support a conclusion whose semantic consequence contradicts the premise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Viruddha (reason proves the opposite; Nyaya example 'Sound is eternal because it is produced' but 'produced' implies non-eternal) is mapped to an architecture decision example: 'Microservices improve independence' justified by evidence that 'every service requires shared database', which contradicts the claim. Derived invariant H-KOS-Contradictory-Reasoning-001.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Equally supported contradictory inferences SHALL remain unresolved until additional evidence changes the epistemic state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Satpratipaksa (competing reasoning: two equally valid-looking arguments) is warned to be a case current AI systems fail at, because they resolve to 'highest probability answer' instead of surfacing conflict. Example: 'Technology X is secure' with Evidence A (audit passed) vs Evidence B (critical vulnerability discovered) should yield KnowledgeState=CONFLICTED, not KnowledgeState=FALSE. Derived invariant H-KOS-Competing-Reasoning-001.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No inference SHALL operate on an unverified entity, property, or relation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Asiddha (unproven premise; Nyaya example a non-existent 'sky-lotus' being fragrant 'because it is a lotus') is called 'the foundation of hallucination', mapped to an LLM inferring 'Framework X has performance issue Y' from 'the company uses Framework X' when that premise was never established. Requires a Premise -> Evidence -> Existence verification -> Inference chain. Derived invariant H-KOS-Premise-Grounding-001.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Higher authority evidence may invalidate a conclusion while preserving historical lineage.
a_rows_sample.statement: Badhita (overridden by stronger evidence; Nyaya example 'Fire is cold because it is a substance', defeated by direct perception) is called 'perhaps the most important for temporal knowledge', mapped to: old knowledge 'Version 1.0 is secure' overridden by new evidence 'Critical CVE discovered'; the old statement is not deleted but transitions Knowledge State VALID -> SUPERSEDED_BY_EVIDENCE. Derived invariant H-KOS-Evidence-Override-001.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Six-Phase Methodology: Samshaya, Pramana, Pancha Avayava, Tarka, Hetvabhasa, Nirnaya
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the six-phase AI-implementation methodology to KnowledgeOS parallels: doubt analysis -> evidence sourcing -> structured reasoning -> contradiction detection -> fallacy detection -> decision/knowledge state.

b_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates six forbidden transitions derived from Tarka Shastra, each paired with the Nyaya parallel that forbids it (apramana, hetvabhasa, tarka-is-apramana, unclassified samsaya, dustarka, the five circular-tarka fallacies).

a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant INV-KOS-004 (Trusted Advancement): canonical knowledge state should advance only through completed and authorized transformations; cites EKS fold model, PKS validation gates, and the ECS hypothesis as evidence candidates.

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-005 Failure Preservation: Failed transformations should preserve the last trusted knowledge state and should NOT create partial authoritative states.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant INV-KOS-005 (Failure Preservation): failed transformations should preserve the last trusted knowledge state and never create partial authoritative states; cites EKS state reconstruction and the ECS publication gate concept as evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-006 Historical Authority: Authoritative knowledge should refer to a validated historical state, not an unverified present condition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant INV-KOS-006 (Historical Authority): authoritative knowledge should refer to a validated historical state, not an unverified present condition; cites ECS, temporal investigation, and EKS durability findings as evidence.

a_rows_sample.statement: Designation reconciliation (ES-005.4): the 'Knowledge Requires Provenance of Knowing' draft candidate is given canonical designation INV-KOS-007; it is claimed to extend H-ZERO-002 (Transformation Origin -- who acted, cited with a 126/126 humanActRef evidence figure from out-of-group archaeology) and INV-003 (Assessment != Authority) toward the 'method' and 'validator' axis of knowing, with Pramana (the means by which knowledge became knowable) as its closest new content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = Neutral starting condition ... It begins as: UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero as neutral knowledge state: Zero != Nothing, it is a neutral starting condition. A new knowledge object begins without authority, evidence, validation or interpretation -- it begins as UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN is proposed as a first-class state, distinct from False and from Missing: UNKNOWN = a known, unresolved state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero lens: UNKNOWN restated as a first-class known-unresolved state, distinct from False and Missing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not force: Unknown -> False / Unknown -> Guess / Unknown -> Empty. Instead: Unknown -> Known Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Combining Zero ('unknown is a valid state') with ECS ('failure does not destroy truth, failure pauses advancement'): Unknown should be preserved and later resolved, never forced into False/Guess/Empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the elephant-and-blind-men story (cited by the source) not as 'everyone is equally right' but as 'different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object', formalized as perspectives A/B/C/D undergoing structural comparison to yield a common invariant = ZERO.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the source's citation of Subhash Kak's six-darsanas-as-cube-walls metaphor into the principle 'knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant', with the research question 'what survives when we rotate the perspective?' answered by ZERO = invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds ... The technology disappears. The invariant remains.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces modal Zero Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds, alongside a claimed prior representation Zero Z_R(K)=invariant across representations and temporal Zero Z_T(K)=invariant across time; illustrated by four possible event-bus technology choices (Kafka/RabbitMQ/sync API/another event bus) all preserving the invariant requirement 'evidence publication must remain replayable' -- the technology disappears, the invariant remains.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = ⋂_i Structure(I_i) ... What structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times, and perspectives? That may be one of our strongest candidates for robust knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as Z=intersection_i Structure(I_i) over interpretations generated from multiple world models W1..Wn (not necessarily literal set intersection in implementation), asking what structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times and perspectives, proposed as one of the strongest candidates for robust knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_i = π_i(R) ... O1 ≠ O2 doesn't necessarily mean R1 ≠ R2. It may simply mean π1 ≠ π2. This gives us a very useful projection lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the elephant analogy as a projection: observation Oi=pi_i(R) for underlying reality/object R and observer perspective pi_i, concluding that differing observations O1!=O2 need not imply differing underlying realities R1!=R2 -- it may simply reflect differing perspectives pi1!=pi2 -- named the 'projection lens'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = Invariant(O1,...,On) ... Zero is not "nothing." It is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Given observations O1..On, defines Z=Invariant(O1,...,On) and explicitly corrects a possible misreading: Zero is not 'nothing', it is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation -- called one of the strongest concepts in the entire exploration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dhātu = transformation structure ... Zero = invariant structure ... what changed? / what remained?
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AF-004 · Zero's chronology inverts CF-005's apparent ordering
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository's 'third sense' of Zero (Z-KOS-001 meta-principle) and the absence-lens sense are BOTH dated 2026-08-22; the goal-gap function sense is the LATEST (2026-08-27 era) — inverting an apparent ordering implied by CF-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-005 · Zero naming collision — a third sense
b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A reference kernel must be able to (1) hold a knowledge state ... Take the transitive dependency closure of those four capabilities ... Is K_4 derived? No. Declared? Not as a governance act. Stipulated as a methodological starting point? YES. ... Status(K_4) = STIPULATED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 4: verifies K4's four capabilities originate from an uncited 'must be able to' Method-paragraph stipulation with no derivation from Theory v1.2, no independent necessity or sufficiency justification found anywhere, and 'must be able to' read as defining implementation scope rather than asserting semantic necessity -- concluding Status(K4)=STIPULATED, while noting the source document is internally honest since it never claims the four themselves (only their closure) are derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_min = {HoldState, TransitionLegally, RejectIllegally, Replay}. Where did that come from? If it is a proposed decomposition, the necessity proof is circular ... proposed capabilities -> test operations against them -> declare operations necessary -- which establishes minimality relative to the chos
b_rows_sample.statement: Sections 1-2: challenges the K_min basis proposed in the immediately preceding document as potentially circular (if K_min is itself a proposed decomposition, testing operations against it and declaring them necessary only shows minimality relative to that chosen capability model, not of the kernel); verifies against readiness/07-MINIMUM-IMPLEMENTABLE-KNOWLEDGEOS.md that K_min's four capabilities are introduced via an uncited, underived 'must be able to' stipulation in a Method paragraph, so the 'excluded by a dependency fact, not by judgement' guarantee covers only the transitive closure OF the four, not the four themselves.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is K_min DERIVED from the corpus, or merely another candidate model? Section 2 already answers half of it: it is stipulated. ... previous 7-blocker conclusion: SUPERSEDED. ... D-1A (compute M_K): BLOCKED -- premature until Level A.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sections 6-7: closes with a status register superseding the prior 7-blocker conclusion and marking K_min as 'CANDIDATE adequacy basis -- UNVALIDATED' given the rival GN-77 basis with better standing, D-1A (computing M_K) as BLOCKED/premature until Level A resolves, and canonical operation freeze as PREMATURE; poses the next required task as a falsification (is K_min derived from the corpus or merely another candidate model, given section 2 already shows it is stipulated) rather than a computation.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'k4-origin-audit-stipulated' POSSIBLY relates to 'kmin-stipulated-not-derived' (batch B0067). Note: Formal origin audit confirming K4's four capabilities are a Method-paragraph stipulation, not derived; the same underlying finding as kmin-stipulated-not-derived (S2790) under a different basis name (K_min = K_4).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_271: KnowledgeOS should define Policy and Assessment at the semantic interface level, while allowing domain-specific policy and measurement regimes to provide their internal evaluation semantics, unless the historical corpus demonstrates that a universal internal structure is required. Status: HYPOTHESIS not theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: States H_271 as the step's key result (explicitly labelled HYPOTHESIS, not theorem), with five falsification criteria (all policies sharing a common formal structure; all assessments requiring one universal scoring model; Policy identity required inside Knowledge State identity; a universal probability model required; domain differences inexpressible via an external regime) and eight required experiments (P1-P8: same-K-different-policy, same-evidence-different-policy, policy-behavioral-equivalence, missing-policy-input, conflicting-policy-rules, score-without-probability, contradictory-evidence, replay-after-policy-change) that are proposed but not executed in this step.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If K1=K2 but Assess(K1,pi1) != Assess(K1,pi2), then Policy cannot be part of the identity of K. This gives: Policy not-in Identity(K), provided the corpus/test evidence confirms the distinction.
b_rows_sample.statement: If two identical knowledge states can be assessed differently under different policies, then Policy is not part of the identity of K -- K represents what the system knows, while pi represents the regime under which that knowledge is evaluated; this is offered conditionally, pending corpus/test confirmation of the antecedent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy identity = behavioral identity, only relative to a declared operation set. ... semantic equality != textual equality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a relative semantic equivalence on policies: pi1==pi2 relative to the KnowledgeOS capability set iff they agree under [[.]]_A on every mandatory assessment operation and under [[.]]_T on every mandatory transformation operation; two textually different policy statements that induce identical behavior under all mandatory operations need not be distinguished by the formal theory, mirroring the state-minimality methodology used for K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H_271: KnowledgeOS should define Policy and Assessment at the semantic interface level, while allowing domain-specific policy and measurement regimes to provide their internal evaluation semantics, unless the historical corpus demonstrates that a universal internal structure is required. Status: HYPOTHESIS not theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: States H_271 as the step's key result (explicitly labelled HYPOTHESIS, not theorem), with five falsification criteria (all policies sharing a common formal structure; all assessments requiring one universal scoring model; Policy identity required inside Knowledge State identity; a universal probability model required; domain differences inexpressible via an external regime) and eight required experiments (P1-P8: same-K-different-policy, same-evidence-different-policy, policy-behavioral-equivalence, missing-policy-input, conflicting-policy-rules, score-without-probability, contradictory-evidence, replay-after-policy-change) that are proposed but not executed in this step.

a_notations: KnowledgeOS Core vs External semantic regimes
b_notations: pi1 == pi2 (behavioral equivalence relative to O_A,O_T)

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kernel-core-vs-external-regime-boundary' POSSIBLY relates to 'policy-semantic-minimality-boundary' (batch B0041). Note: A proposed architectural boundary listing Knowledge State/Assertion/Relation/Identity/History/Transformation-interface/Evidence-interface/Assessment-interface/invariants as core, versus policy rules/measurement models/statistical models/domain thresholds/assessment criteria/governance rules as external regimes; explicitly a hypothesis pending corpus audit confirmation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest set of genuinely irreducible epistemic capabilities required for KnowledgeOS to support the required knowledge lifecycle? ... This is a MINIMALITY / ABLATION experiment. It is NOT a naming exercise.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the primary research question as a formal ablation experiment over candidate operator set C0 (13 operators), explicitly distinguishing it from naming exercises, aesthetic simplification, universal-necessity claims, or retrofitting existing architecture, and requiring provenance tagging ([CORPUS]/[EXT]/[INF]/[PROP]/[EXP]/[NEG]/[OPEN]) with no silent promotion to canon.

a_rows_sample.anchor: if the proposed implementation merely changes Discriminate into DiscriminateIncludingGapDetection, then DetectGap has NOT actually been eliminated. That is semantic smuggling.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines 'semantic smuggling' as the critical failure mode of the whole experiment: claiming an operator is reducible by silently renaming its function into a remaining operator (e.g. Remove DetectGap, redefine Validate to also detect gaps) rather than genuinely composing it from independent semantics -- requires an explicit SMUGGLING=TRUE/FALSE flag with justification for every proposed reduction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Cardinality minimality ... B. Semantic minimality ... C. Compositional minimality ... D. Architectural minimality ... E. Cognitive universality. Do NOT assume these are equivalent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five non-equivalent senses of kernel 'minimality' (cardinality; semantic -- no operator removable without losing an irreducible capability; compositional -- every retained operator contributes something non-reproducible by composition of others; architectural -- no separate responsibility introduced when naturally derivable from another; cognitive universality -- required by every epistemic system), designating semantic+compositional minimality as the primary experimental target and cardinality as only secondary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C1 acquire an observation ... C24 support learning from new observations. These are INITIAL capabilities. ... Do not optimize the capability list merely to make the operator set smaller.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 24-item capability space (C1-C24, spanning observation acquisition, meaning construction, representation, relation, discrimination, hypothesis formation, inference, gap detection, challenge, validation, revision, inquiry-adequacy determination, action selection, context/temporal/uncertainty/assumption representation, provenance and alternative preservation, non-identifiability support, observation-vs-interpretation distinction, representation-independent semantic equivalence, smallest-adequate-answer production, and learning from new observations) that must be derived independently of the candidate operator names, not by restating them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: oi : S_i -> S_j where S_i and S_j are abstract epistemic states/artifacts. Do not assume all operators act directly on K_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes candidate operators as typed transformations over explicitly distinct carrier types (Observation, Evidence, SemanticRepresentation, Hypothesis, Model, Claim, AlternativeSet, RequirementSet, EpistemicState, DecisionProposal), explicitly rejecting the assumption that every operator acts directly on K_t, and requires every proposed composite reduction o_removed=f(o_remaining) to be documented across nine dimensions (input/output type, preconditions, postconditions, semantic/epistemic effect, information loss, introduced assumptions, and whether removed semantics were secretly embedded elsewhere).

a_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO 7 — Missing evidence ... Expected possibility: cannot determine. ... SCENARIO 12 — Smallest adequate answer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a 16-scenario canonical test suite grounded in concrete Nexus-infrastructure examples (basic/numeric/network observation; conflicting evidence; ambiguous semantics like 'the server is available'; temporal revision without conflating historical and current-state equality; missing evidence legitimately yielding 'cannot determine'; competing partially-supported hypotheses; model criticism; context-dependent semantic interpretation; inquiry-relative adequacy; smallest adequate answer; cost-constrained action selection; non-identifiability; provenance conflict; representation equivalence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Build a SMALL RESEARCH SIMULATOR. ... Do NOT claim this is the canonical KnowledgeOS state model. Label it: [PROP] experimental state representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires building a small, explicitly non-production research simulator over an explicitly [PROP]-labelled experimental epistemic state K_t=(claims,representations,relations,evidence,provenance,assumptions,alternatives,uncertainty,context,history), with every helper function classified (domain operator / data-structure operation / infrastructure utility / test harness / serialization) so that only genuine domain operators count toward kernel size.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Leave-one-out is not sufficient. Some operators may be individually removable but jointly necessary. ... pairwise ablation; ... selected triple ablations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires pairwise and higher-order ablation beyond simple leave-one-out, explicitly anticipating that some operators may be individually removable yet jointly necessary (synergy, substitution, hidden dependency, or operator bundles) -- illustrated by Interpret+Represent potentially being coupled without necessarily being one operator, requiring a typed factorization test rather than an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROPERTY P2 — Non-identifiability: If evidence cannot distinguish H1 and H2, the system must not fabricate a unique determination. ... PROPERTY P7 — No information creation: Processing existing evidence cannot create unsupported empirical information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ten falsifiable properties (P1-P10) for randomized property-based simulation testing: revision-representability under contradicting evidence, non-fabrication under non-identifiability, provenance preservation, temporal consistency (no erasure of historical truth), semantic distinction preserved when evidence does not resolve it, adequacy != mere answer-existence, no information creation from pure processing, alternative preservation absent evidence-based elimination, context-sensitivity of relevance, and challenge-required-before-validated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT interpret a 99% scenario success rate as proof of correctness. ... Statistics support robustness assessment; they do not prove minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes disciplined statistical treatment: separate deterministic logical failures from stochastic/implementation/model-specification/conceptual failures, report failure rates and robustness across seeds and sensitivity to definitional choices rather than a single aggregate score, and explicitly distinguishes the statistical robustness question (p_hat_failure) from the logical necessity question (exists x: Reach(S,x) != Reach(S union {o},x)) -- statistics inform robustness, they do not establish minimality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But do NOT equate: information quantity = knowledge. ... Do NOT equate: Pi_t = K_t. ... fit != validation, regression != causality, estimation != identification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the experiment to run information-theoretic checks (data-processing inequality, sufficient representation) without equating information quantity with knowledge, probabilistic checks (Pi_t=L(X|F_t) without Pi_t=K_t) across six specified uncertainty scenarios, and a causal/model-criticism check enforcing fit!=validation, regression!=causality, estimation!=identification as three explicitly distinct failure classes a model must not conflate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = predicate ... Ideal State = state/target construct ... Inquiry = domain input ... Governance = external constraint ... Authorization = governance mechanism ... Select = decision/action mechanism. But these are hypotheses. Test them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a DDD pass over every candidate operator asking whether it is a genuine domain capability owning a distinct invariant/responsibility, or instead a policy, state predicate, or orchestration concern -- explicitly naming Zero, Ideal State, Inquiry, Governance, Authorization, and Select as operators whose kernel membership must be tested rather than assumed, offering (only as hypotheses) demotions of each to a non-operator role.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not conclude: 'Operator X is necessary because the current KnowledgeOS architecture already has X.' That would be circular.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids architectural circularity as a justification for kernel membership (existing class != domain primitive; existing service != kernel operator; existing workflow != epistemic necessity), requiring the experiment to reason from domain capabilities and epistemic requirements rather than from current implementation structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 — Representation failure ... F19 — Implementation artifact ... F20 — Simulator artifact. Do not call F19/F20 kernel failures. ... Never manufacture a positive result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a twenty-category failure taxonomy (F1-F20) for classifying ablation failures, explicitly excluding implementation and simulator artifacts (F19/F20) from counting as genuine kernel failures, and mandates that negative results ('removing X did not break anything', 'no meaningful conclusion can currently be drawn') be treated as first-class, valid, and never suppressed in favor of manufactured positive findings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Search for multiple Pareto candidates. ... Do not collapse these into one arbitrary weighted score.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires searching for multiple Pareto-optimal candidate kernels (not one single smallest kernel) evaluated along nine uncollapsed axes (cardinality, semantic coverage, compositionality, coupling, interpretability, falsifiability, domain cohesion, implementation independence, evidence strength), with any weighted composite score requiring an explicit sensitivity analysis over weight choices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: find S subset-of O such that C_required subset-of Reach(S) and forall o in S: C_required not-subset-of Reach(S \ {o}). ... Reach(S) ... must be defined carefully.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes semantic minimality as a set-system reachability problem: find a minimal operator subset S such that all required capabilities are reachable by valid typed compositions of S, and no operator in S can be removed without breaking that containment -- explicitly cautioning that the Reach(S) composition function must be defined by explicit, non-arbitrary rules rather than declared to include whatever the researcher wishes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Empirically necessary ... Formally necessary ... DDD-necessary ... These can disagree. ... That is a very interesting result -- not a contradiction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three independent necessity tests (empirical: the simulator cannot run without it; formal: no valid composition of remaining operators supplies it; DDD: the responsibility is a genuinely distinct domain concept) that can legitimately disagree without contradiction, illustrated by Select potentially being computationally derivable from Determine while DDD analysis still separates epistemic determination from action selection as distinct responsibilities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 01-research-question.md ... 03-capability-model.md ... 04-operator-contracts.md ... 05-operator-capability-matrix.md ... 06-composition-rules.md ... FINAL-kernel-reduction-report.md
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes a fixed 18-file experimental output directory (docs/knowledgeos/research/kernel-reduction/), explicitly forbidding modification of canonical architecture documents and requiring the simulator code to be isolated in an experimental directory -- this file naming scheme directly matches several files this same batch reads (01-research-question.md, 03-capability-model.md, 04-operator-contracts.md, 05-operator-capability-matrix.md, 06-composition-rules.md), identifying this prompt as their likely originating mandate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would consider the experiment successful even if Claude concludes: 'The 13 operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because the semantic granularity of the candidate operators is unstable.' ... What is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive?
a_rows_sample.statement: Names as potentially the single most valuable possible experimental outcome a finding that the 13 candidate operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because their semantic granularity is itself unstable -- reframing the open research problem from 'which operator to delete' to 'what is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive', and explicitly allows the kernel to turn out structurally different from a flat operator set (e.g. K=(S,T,O) or K=(P,R,delta), or some operators turning out to be predicates like Zero rather than transformations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's binding authorization boundary: it is explicitly research-only, not authorized to canonize a kernel, and no result may be promoted to invariant/theorem/ADR/standard by the document itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What this experiment is NOT: a naming exercise ... a retrofit of the current architecture: Part XXIV "existing class != domain primitive" — no architectural circularity ... a canonization.
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates six things the experiment explicitly is not (naming exercise, aesthetic minimization, a vote, a universal-necessity proof, an architectural retrofit/circularity, or a canonization), each tied to a concrete safeguard already built into the executed model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: They disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Those disagreements are results, not defects.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports, as an executed finding, that the three distinct necessity notions (empirically necessary, formally necessary via the reach algebra, and DDD-necessary as a distinct domain responsibility) disagree for the operators Select, Discriminate, and Revise, explicitly framing the disagreement itself as a valid experimental result rather than a flaw in the model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment targets B + C. A result that improves A while worsening B/C is reported as a worse result, per the protocol's final principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms semantic minimality (B) and compositional minimality (C) as the experiment's primary targets, with cardinality (A) explicitly subordinate: an improvement in operator count that worsens semantic or compositional minimality is scored as a worse result overall.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Modification M-1 — C25 added [CORPUS]. ... Without C25, C10 is unrealizable in any model where a Verdict requires evidence ... This modification enlarges the required capability set and therefore makes minimization harder, not easier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds a new capability C25 ('admit an observation as evidence under a policy') to the protocol's original 24-item list, justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) combined with prior constraint 9 (information != evidence) means no capability in C1-C24 covers the observation-to-evidence transition, making C10 (validate) unrealizable without it -- explicitly noted as making minimization harder, not more convenient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C18 reclassified as NON-DISCRIMINATING [NEG]. ... no operator set can fail C18 in this simulator. ... This is a limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies capability C18 (preserve provenance) as non-discriminating because the reach engine structurally guarantees provenance via its derivation DAG for every artifact regardless of operator set, making it untestable by leave-one-out -- explicitly reported as a limitation of the measuring instrument, not a substantive finding about the kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C20 given an explicit failure mode: the system must be able to hold >=2 hypotheses and return an UNDECIDED discrimination. It can then fail by overreach — producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives it is determining between.
b_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the under-specified capability C20 (support non-identifiability) with a concrete, falsifiable failure mode (overreach: producing a Determination without being able to represent >=2 held alternatives with an UNDECIDED verdict), preventing the capability from being trivially 'supported' by doing nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: merge C2 and C3 (meaning + representation) | corpus explicitly separates Observation != Proposition != Knowledge; merging is tested instead as robustness variant V1 ... merge C12 and C13 (determine + select) | different carriers, different inputs (Inquiry vs Objective); tested as V5
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports two considered-and-rejected capability-model modifications (merging meaning-construction with representation; merging determination with action-selection), each rejected on corpus-grounded or type-grounded reasons but retained as explicit robustness variants (V1, V5) to be tested rather than silently discarded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms ... 'redefine Y so that Y also does X' is mechanically detectable — it is a change to Y's atom set, i.e. a change to the model, not a composition within it -> SMUGGLING = TRUE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the anti-circularity device at the heart of the executed experiment: an operator is identified purely by its declared set of semantic atoms, consulted by the reach engine to the exclusion of operator names, so that redefining one operator to secretly absorb another's function becomes a detectable change to the atom-set model itself (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a legitimate composition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Atoms are deliberately allowed to be shared. A 1:1 operator->atom assignment would make every operator irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous. Two atoms are shared ... and that sharing is where all the interesting results live.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explains why two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared between operators rather than assigning each operator a unique atom: a strict 1:1 mapping would make every operator trivially irreducible by construction, rendering the whole ablation experiment vacuous -- the shared atoms are identified as the source of the experiment's most interesting results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structural concerns (context, time, uncertainty, assumption, provenance, alternatives) are modelled as invariants checked over the reach closure ... not as ownable powers. Making them ownable would have handed one operator a monopoly on, e.g., provenance, and rigged the result.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that structural concerns (context/time/uncertainty/assumptions/provenance/alternatives) are deliberately modelled as invariants checked over the whole reach closure rather than as atoms any single operator could own, to avoid rigging the ablation result by handing one operator an artificial monopoly on a cross-cutting concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: difference-decision ∈ {Discriminate, DetectGap}; norm-comparison ∈ {DetectGap, Determine}. DetectGap holds no atom exclusively. ... it is the assumption most responsible for the headline result, and it is therefore attacked directly by robustness variant V4.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies DetectGap as the only operator in C0-union-Qualify holding no atom exclusively (both its atoms, difference-decision and norm-comparison, are shared with Discriminate and Determine respectively), flagging this modelling choice as the single assumption most responsible for the experiment's headline redundancy result, and explicitly scheduling it for direct attack under robustness variant V4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observe | world-contact | the sole channel for empirical content; nothing downstream may create it | STRONG ... Represent | symbolic-encoding | make semantic content manipulable without asserting it | WEAK ... Qualify | evidential-qualification | admit an observation as evidence under a policy | STR
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the full per-operator contract table (13 C0 operators plus Qualify), each with its claimed atom(s), non-reducible responsibility, and a corpus-support grade from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Relate, Select).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Discriminate and DetectGap are all-zero rows. Neither is required by any capability under leave-one-out, because each covers the other's shared atoms. That is not evidence that the capabilities are unneeded — it is evidence that the operator packaging is redundant.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's headline finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are both all-zero rows in the leave-one-out operator-capability matrix, since each can cover the other's shared atoms when the other is removed -- explicitly interpreted not as evidence the underlying capabilities are unneeded but as evidence that the CURRENT OPERATOR PACKAGING of those capabilities is redundant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C5 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} both removed | the atom difference-decision. C8 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} or {DetectGap, Determine} removed | difference-decision + norm-comparison. A leave-one-out matrix alone would have declared C5 and C8 unnecessary. They are not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that capabilities C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero columns under leave-one-out and become irreducible only under pairwise ablation (C5 lost only when both Discriminate and DetectGap are removed together; C8 lost when either {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are removed together), concretely demonstrating that a leave-one-out-only analysis would have wrongly certified both capabilities as unnecessary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A carrier kind is not stamped by the operator that produced it. It is derived from (multiset of input kinds, atoms introduced by this step) -> kind ... Otherwise 'only DetectGap can make a Gap' would be true by fiat and the ablation rigged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a second anti-circularity device: a derived carrier's kind is determined purely by its input-kind multiset and the atoms introduced, never by which operator produced it, so that any operator set capable of introducing the required atoms over the required inputs can produce a given carrier -- preventing the ablation from being rigged by fiat operator-carrier ownership.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim is producible only via entailment — so its warrant kind is DEDUCTIVE by construction. A Verdict produced by generate-and-test is not a Claim. This is what keeps Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize an honest question rather than a definitional trick.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes, from the carrier-derivation table's type rules, that a Claim can only be produced via the entailment atom (making its warrant kind deductive by construction) while a Verdict produced by generate-and-test (Hypothesize then Validate) is a structurally different carrier -- keeping the composition question 'is Infer equivalent to Validate composed with Hypothesize' a genuinely open, honest question rather than one settled by definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict requires Evidence. This is where the absence of Qualify from C0 becomes fatal. ... Determination requires both NormDelta (hence IdealState) and Inquiry — encoding prior constraint 5, that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives from the type system that a Verdict carrier requires an Evidence input, making the corpus's unimplemented Qualify operator (excluded from C0) fatal to realizing validation without it; separately derives that a Determination carrier requires both a NormDelta (itself requiring IdealState) and an Inquiry, formally encoding the prior constraint that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative directly into the type system rather than merely asserting it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reach(S) = mu A . AMBIENT union {k | exists o in S : k in derive(A, o.atoms)}. Monotone, terminating (finite carrier set), and independent of operator names.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Reach(S) as the least fixpoint (over a finite carrier set, hence terminating and monotone) of applying available operators' atoms to the ambient carriers, with a capability achieved iff its required carrier kinds and atoms are both covered by Reach(S) and the atom pool of S -- the operational definition of formal necessity used throughout the experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No helper functions. ... No helper performs the work of a removed operator — a claim that is mechanically checkable, since helpers cannot introduce atoms.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the reach engine's implementation contains only domain-operator applications plus generic data-structure operations (set union, fixpoint computation), with every helper function classified per the protocol's requirement, and that no helper can perform the work of a removed operator because helpers structurally cannot introduce atoms -- making the no-semantic-smuggling guarantee mechanically checkable rather than merely asserted.

a_aliases: Claude Code CLI Prompt -- KnowledgeOS Kernel Reduction & Minimality Experiment

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kernel-reduction-experiment-KR-2026-09-01-executed-results' POSSIBLY relates to 'kernel-reduction-ablation-experiment-protocol' (batch B0056). Note: The actual EXECUTED research output of the kernel-reduction/minimality experiment mandated by this batch's own prompt document (kernel-reduction-ablation-experiment-protocol), explicitly labelled [EXP] research, not architecture/governance/canon, with an authorization boundary stating this lane cannot canonize a kernel. Tests the candidate 13-operator set C0={Observe,Interpret,Represent,Relate,Discriminate,Hypothesize,Infer,DetectGap,Challenge,Validate,Revise,Determine,Select} plus Qualify (held outside C0). Builds a formal, mechanically-checked anti-circularity apparatus: an operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms (14 atoms: world-contact, meaning-assignment, symbolic-encoding, relational-linking, difference-decision, content-generation, entailment, norm-comparison, adversarial-negation, warrant-assessment, state-mutation, closure-judgment, preference-over-actions, evidential-qualification), so 'redefine Y to secretly also do X' becomes a mechanically detectable change to Y's atom set (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a valid composition; atoms are deliberately allowed to be SHARED (two atoms are shared: difference-decision between Discriminate/DetectGap, and norm-comparison between DetectGap/Determine) since a 1:1 operator-to-atom mapping would make the experiment vacuous by construction. Defines a typed carrier-derivation table (ambient carriers: World/Context/Inquiry/IdealState/Policy/Rule/Objective/ActionSet/EpistemicState(K_t) -- none produced by any operator; derived carriers: Observation/SemanticContent/Representation/Evidence/Relation/Discrimination/Hypothesis/Claim/Defeater/Verdict/NormDelta/Gap/Determination/Decision) where a carrier kind is derived from (input-kind multiset, atoms introduced) rather than stamped by whichever operator produced it, formalizing Reach(S) as a monotone, terminating least fixpoint over ambient carriers -- deliberately excluding any hand-added 'obvious' closures or helper functions that could smuggle in a removed operator's work. Produces a 25-capability model (the protocol's C1-C24 plus a NEWLY ADDED C25 'admit an observation as evidence under a policy', justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) means C10's Verdict-requires-Evidence type rule is otherwise unrealizable -- an addition that makes minimization HARDER, not easier, so cannot be a convenience), with C18 (provenance) explicitly marked NON-DISCRIMINATING (structurally guaranteed by the reach engine's derivation-DAG bookkeeping, hence untestable by this instrument -- an explicit limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel) and C20 (non-identifiability) operationalized with an explicit overreach failure mode (holding >=2 hypotheses plus returning UNDECIDED; failing by producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives). Computes an operator x capability matrix via actual leave-one-out removal-and-reevaluation (not asserted), yielding the experiment's headline empirical finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are BOTH ALL-ZERO ROWS under leave-one-out (neither is individually required for any capability, because each covers the other's shared atoms) -- explicitly NOT evidence the capabilities are unneeded but evidence the OPERATOR PACKAGING IS REDUNDANT; correspondingly C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero COLUMNS under leave-one-out and only become irreducible under PAIRWISE ablation (C5 lost only if {Discriminate,DetectGap} are BOTH removed, at the shared atom difference-decision; C8 lost if {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are both removed, at difference-decision+norm-comparison) -- concluding a leave-one-out matrix alone would have wrongly declared C5/C8 unnecessary, which is the concrete justification for why pairwise ablation is mandatory and cardinality is only a secondary result. Confirms via the type system that Claim is producible ONLY via entailment (making its warrant kind DEDUCTIVE by construction, so a Verdict from generate-and-test is never a Claim, keeping 'Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize' a genuine open question rather than a definitional trick), that Verdict requires Evidence (making the corpus's absent Qualify function fatal to any C0-only realization), and that Determination requires BOTH NormDelta (hence IdealState) AND Inquiry (encoding the prior constraint that Ideal State is inquiry-relative). Formally distinguishes three notions of operator necessity that can and do disagree without being a defect -- empirically necessary (scenario/simulation fails without it), formally necessary (no valid composition of the rest supplies it via Reach), and DDD-necessary (a distinct domain responsibility) -- explicitly reporting they disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Rates per-operator corpus support from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-a-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Select, Relate).
