Note: Re-registered in B0057 to satisfy this batch label-registration check; this batch (S2347-S2354, S2356, S2361-S2366, S2380-S2381) reads the direct continuation (parts VII-XXVI) of the same KR-2026-09-01 experiment whose first sections (01,03,04,05,06) B0056 already registered under this label. relation_to_existing copied unchanged from the B0056 original proposal per cross-batch identity discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DI principle vs framework import: adopt the DI/composition-root principle without adopting Spring — the corpus wants the first, but the kernel file pairs the principle with the Spring runtime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
b_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
b_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
b_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
b_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledge-claim-root-object-question' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-kernel-concept' (batch B0010). Note: Proposed in S0367 as possibly the more fundamental root domain object than Kernel/Knowledge/KnowledgeAggregate -- the domain object whose integrity KnowledgeOS actually protects -- with two competing candidate shapes sketched but left unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a knowledge repository. It is not a search system. It is not an AI oracle. It is a constitutional epistemic system that protects and improves the process by which justified knowledge emerges.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines KnowledgeOS's character negatively (not a repository/search system/AI oracle) and positively as a constitutional epistemic system that protects and improves the process by which justified knowledge emerges.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge dimensions must evolve independently unless an explicit transformation connects them.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a 'dimension purity' law: Evidence changing does not automatically change Authority; Confidence increasing does not mean Truth increases; AI-generated text is not Observation; Decision is not Knowledge. KnowledgeOS prevents dimension collapse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Memory of reasoning ... not only: Memory of information. It preserves the path to knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS is framed as a 'reasoning memory' that preserves why, from where, using what evidence, with what assumptions, under which context, at what time, and through what reasoning a conclusion was reached -- not only the conclusion itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown | Observation | Evidence | Hypothesis | Reasoning | Assessment | Validated Knowledge | Revision | New Understanding. The old state is not deleted. It becomes history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes an epistemic lifecycle stage sequence (Unknown->Observation->Evidence->Hypothesis->Reasoning->Assessment->Validated Knowledge->Revision->New Understanding) and asserts the old state is never deleted, only historicized.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The first state is: 'I do not yet know.' This is not weakness. It is epistemic honesty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge begins from a neutral 'Unknown' state rather than an assumed-true state, credited to 'the Zero principle'; framed as epistemic honesty rather than weakness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The system records: CONFLICTED instead of forcing: TRUE / FALSE prematurely.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a normal database ('which value is correct?') with KnowledgeOS ('why do different perspectives disagree?'): Claim A + Evidence A and Claim B + Evidence B may coexist as CONFLICTED rather than forcing a premature TRUE/FALSE resolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A conclusion must never become an observation. Especially: AI generated answer != Fact from reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observed reality -> Evidence -> Reasoning -> Conclusion are different epistemic categories; a conclusion must never become an observation, and an AI-generated answer must never be treated as a fact from reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Meaning + Context = Knowledge. Removing context destroys knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Meaning does not exist independently of context (example: 'The system is cold' could mean a temperature problem, unfriendly behavior, or a market slowdown); Meaning + Context = Knowledge, and removing context destroys knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But: Revision != Deletion. The historical reasoning remains.
a_rows_sample.statement: A truth-seeking system must allow itself to be wrong: accepted knowledge can be revised in light of new evidence, but revision is never deletion -- historical reasoning remains.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge -> Assessment -> Decision -> Action. The system preserves: 'Why was this action justified at that time?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge does not directly execute; it flows through Assessment and Decision before Action, and the system preserves why an action was justified at the time it was taken.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematics describes the structure. It does not create the structure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Topology (invariants/transformations), lattices (partial ordering), temporal logic (validity over time), graphs (relationships), and sheaf-like thinking (local/global consistency) are useful as descriptive tools; claims like 'KnowledgeOS is a complex number' or 'is a formula' are rejected -- mathematics describes structure, it does not define it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If KnowledgeOS were a person, it would be: A careful scientist + historian + judge ... Philosopher ... Engineer
a_rows_sample.statement: Personifies KnowledgeOS's character as a composite: Scientist ('what evidence supports this?'), Historian ('how did this belief evolve?'), Judge ('what authority process justified this?'), Philosopher ('what does this actually mean?'), Engineer ('can this transformation happen safely?').

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a constitutional epistemic system designed to preserve the integrity of knowledge evolution... It does not manufacture truth; it creates the conditions where trustworthy truth can emerge, survive transformation, and improve through continuous reasoning and revision.
a_rows_sample.statement: First 'Final Character Statement': KnowledgeOS preserves the integrity of knowledge evolution by maintaining separation between meaning, evidence, authority, context, time, reasoning, and action; it creates conditions for trustworthy truth rather than manufacturing truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A KnowledgeOS kernel is not a container for knowledge. It is a protector of the relationships that make knowledge trustworthy... KnowledgeOS protects the path from observation to justified understanding.
a_rows_sample.statement: A second, shorter essence statement: the kernel is a protector of relationships that make knowledge trustworthy, and it protects the path from observation to justified understanding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. What exists? ... 2. Why should we believe it? ... 3. Who produced this understanding? ... 4. How does it change? ... 5. What can be done with it?
a_rows_sample.statement: Restructures the character model into five constitutional questions, each preserving a dimension group: Identity (semantic identity/context/meaning/lineage), Evidence/Justification (observations/evidence/reasoning/contradictions/assumptions), Epistemic Agency (observer/analyst/reasoner/validator/authority source), Transformation/Time (evolution/revisions/supersession/historical states), Decision Relationship (decisions influenced/actions justified/consequences).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is the constitutional epistemic substrate that preserves the integrity of the relationship between the Knower, the Known, the Evidence, and the transformations through which justified understanding evolves over time.
a_rows_sample.statement: A refined one-sentence essence statement, explicitly offered as an improvement over a prior version that named only 'the Knower, the Known, and the Path of Reasoning'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not say 'the kernel is ready to be written in stone.' ... Research insight -> Candidate invariant -> Cross-domain validation -> Established invariant -> Kernel law ... Kernel laws are not yet finalized.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against prematurely declaring the kernel finalized: the discovery phase produced a strong candidate model, but the established discipline requires research insight to pass through candidate-invariant, cross-domain-validation, and established-invariant stages before becoming kernel law; status recorded as character definition/invariant candidates/kernel boundary/research lenses all 'mature' but kernel laws explicitly 'not yet finalized'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Before Tarka: KnowledgeOS preserves trustworthy knowledge evolution. After Tarka: KnowledgeOS preserves the conditions under which reasoning can transform evidence into trustworthy knowledge... Tarka explains that the middle part cannot be a black box.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the character statement to foreground reasoning as the (previously implicit, black-boxed) middle step between Evidence and Knowledge conclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reasoning is a governed transformation ... Input: Evidence + Context + Existing Knowledge -> Transformation: Reasoning Process -> Output: Derived Knowledge State. Not: Evidence -> Magic AI -> Truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a new principle: KnowledgeOS must treat reasoning as a governed transformation with explicit inputs (evidence, context, existing knowledge) and outputs (derived knowledge state), explicitly rejecting an opaque 'Evidence -> Magic AI -> Truth' model.

b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematics should describe, not define: invariants must be discovered from observed knowledge behavior first, and mathematical structures found afterward to describe them -- never the reverse order.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

a_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
a_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article I.1 ... Article I.2 ... Article I.3 -- Mathematics describes, never defines.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter I, the Constitutional Identity: Article I.1 the character (KnowledgeOS governs how knowledge is created/justified/transformed/challenged/evolved while preserving identity/context/evidence/authority/reasoning/uncertainty/agency/historical evolution); Article I.2 the three clause refinements (existence, reasoning, identity) are constitutionally absorbed as phrasing refinements, not supersessions; Article I.3 the governing maxim 'Mathematics describes, never defines' -- topology, type theory, graphs, TMS, AGM, LLMs are mechanisms/explanatory lenses, never kernel law by virtue of being mathematical or computational.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONSTITUTIONAL KERNEL <- the eleven articles (PRESERVE) ... Engine Layer (GOVERN) ... Mechanisms (GOVERN) ... Representations (ENABLE) ... Implementation (ENABLE)
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter III, the Kernel Boundary: a 5-tier diagram -- Constitutional Kernel (the 11 articles, PRESERVE) served by Engine Layer (validation engines, fallacy detection, debate pipeline, intent classification, verdict vocabulary, GOVERN), Mechanisms (epistemic-inquiry lifecycle, reasoning pipelines, GOVERN), Representations (evidence records, context tuples, epistemic state model, absence taxonomy, epistemic graph, typed encodings, ENABLE), and Implementation (storage, interfaces, systems, deliberately unconstrained, ENABLE). III.1 the kernel does not do the reasoning -- it states what must be preserved/never collapse; engines execute governed transformations realizing those constraints. III.2 no engine/mechanism/representation may violate an article -- evolution that violates an article is a corruption, not an evolution, subject to Chapter V. III.3 implementation is deliberately out of constitutional scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V.1 Engineering evolution -- no amendment required. ... V.2 Constitutional amendment -- required ... V.3 What amendment MAY do ... V.4 Ratification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter V, Amendment Discipline (new content, not present verbatim in any prior artifact in this file group): engines/mechanisms/representations/implementation (Chapter III) MAY evolve freely provided no evolution violates an article (V.1); the 11 articles, the character, the negative boundary, and the kernel/engine boundary SHALL NOT change except by HPA-ratified constitutional amendment, and no article SHALL be weakened (V.2); amendment MAY refine wording, correct inconsistency, or -- on evidence a specific corruption is unguarded -- add a strengthening clause, but SHALL NOT add new concepts/sources/rows ('the corpus that produced this Constitution is closed; adding knowledge to the kernel would violate the discipline this Constitution establishes', V.3); amendment is effective only by HPA ruling following the same evidence/domain-independence/necessity/failure-test discipline that produced step 5 (V.4).

NON-AUTHORITATIVE pending HPA ratification, formalizing (adding nothing to) the step-5 selection; the register remains 25 candidates + 4 Established unchanged, the 11 articles being the selection and the register the record of how it was reached; upon ratification it becomes the governing instrument for Reference Architecture and Implementation Model, which SHALL conform to it and SHALL NOT extend it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 1 — Identity ... Representation SHALL NOT become meaning. Similarity SHALL NOT become identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No new concepts · no new rows · no new philosophy

a_rows_sample.anchor: Amendment discipline — because this is a constitutional document, define: what can change · what requires constitutional amendment · what is merely engineering evolution

b_rows_sample.statement: The eleven laws are the constitutional boundary the Constitution formalizes exactly, with the two SS2a/2b merges resolved -- no law added, removed, or weakened; no new concepts/rows/philosophy ('The system has reached the point where adding more knowledge would violate the very discipline it is trying to establish' -- HPA verbatim); the register stands at 25 candidates + 4 Established, unchanged; character head 43 stands, with its three clause refinements already adjudicated (P4) and available without re-adjudication; the kernel/engine boundary is fixed (11 laws = kernel/PRESERVE; validation engines, fallacy detection, debate pipeline, lifecycle stages, intent classification, evidence schemas, context tuples, state model, absence taxonomy, epistemic graph, and mathematical lenses are deferred mechanisms, referenceable but never part of the kernel); the five non-identities carry into the Constitution unchanged as the negative boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EXPERIMENT ID KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09 ... Determine whether there is any reproducible empirical or structural relationship between: A. elimination/Transformation-relative Zero, B. representation preservation/adequacy. WITHOUT assuming that Zero is a preservation criterion. ... The exp
a_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09, a bridge/falsification experiment explicitly designed to determine whether there is any reproducible relationship between elimination/Transformation-relative Zero and representation-preservation adequacy without assuming Zero is a preservation criterion, required to remain capable of falsifying the hypothesized relationship, and prohibited from constructing an algebra, pre-selecting a carrier, modifying Theory v1.2, creating Theory v1.3, selecting a kernel operator, or merging KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION into one formalism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: ~89.7% singleton-determined levels ... ~8.2% irreducible levels ... Does NOT establish Zero as a preservation criterion. KR-REP-REDUCTION: R5 adequate, R4 inadequate ... Found no observed Zero/boundary association in that experiment. Does NOT establish a KR-ZERO law. ... These experiments a
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the existing empirical baseline the bridge experiment builds on: KR-ZERO (89.7% singleton-determined, 8.2% irreducible, does not establish Zero as a preservation criterion) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (R5 adequate/R4 inadequate, no observed Zero/boundary association), framed as complementary but analytically independent results whose missing bridge the new experiment must test rather than assume.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H0: Zero and preservation are not systematically related in the tested regime. H1: Zero is associated with preservation under specified conditions. H2: Zero is predictive of preservation only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations. H3: Any apparent relationship is explain
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies four competing hypotheses to be distinguished -- H0 no systematic relationship, H1 association under specified conditions, H2 predictive only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations, H3 apparent relationship explained by a confounding factor (transformation class, contract, observable, redundancy, representation regime) -- with an explicit instruction not to privilege H1, and defines success as producing a clear positive or negative result regarding the tested relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: USE A PARALLEL REPRESENTATION FAMILY. Do NOT use only a deterministic sequential chain. A sequential chain ... has a data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn) <= H(Q|R(n-1)) and therefore cannot test non-monotone adequacy. The present experiment requires independently generated representations: Ra = Ta(D),
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the critical design rule that the bridge experiment use a parallel representation family (independently generated representations Ra=Ta(D), Rb=Tb(D), neither a deterministic function of the other) rather than only a deterministic sequential chain, since a sequential chain's data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn)<=H(Q|R(n-1)) structurally prevents testing non-monotone adequacy -- directly addressing the H-C category error found in the prior KR-REP-REDUCTION reviews.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mathematical carrier must be the minimum structure required by the actual experiment. Do not declare: set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra as the carrier before the experiment. ... clearly distinguish: experimental carrier, mathematical ca
a_rows_sample.statement: Prohibits declaring any specific mathematical carrier (set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra) before the experiment runs, requiring the carrier to be the minimum structure the experiment actually needs, and mandates keeping experimental carrier, mathematical carrier, and future KnowledgeOS knowledge representation explicitly distinct with no unevidenced transfer between them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use a finite structured source D ... rich enough to permit: redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, preservation and information-loss cases. ... For every source case store D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation para
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the source data D to be a finite, deterministically-seeded structured source rich enough to permit redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, and both preservation and information-loss cases, with complete persistence of every source case's D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation parameters, Zero ground truth, every representation, adequacy result, and decoder result, so no result depends on regenerated or hidden data.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum construct representations with: R_A: information-preserving transformation, R_B: controlled lossy transformation, R_C: redundancy-removing transformation, R_D: relational/context-sensitive transformation. ... Do not optimize transformations after seeing results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires at minimum four independently constructed representations -- R_A (information-preserving), R_B (controlled lossy), R_C (redundancy-removing), R_D (relational/context-sensitive) -- each fully specified (transformation ID, mathematical definition, input/output type, deterministic/random status, seed, provenance, expected information effect, contract dependencies) before results are examined, with no post-hoc optimization of transformations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define Q BEFORE generating representations. ... Adequate(R) iff Q is recoverable from R. Operationally measure both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and exact semantic violation count Nviol ... Do not treat Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof that population H(Q|R)=0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the preservation target Q to be defined before representations are generated, with adequacy defined as Q being recoverable from R, measured operationally via both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and an exact semantic violation count Nviol, while never treating the empirical Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof of the population-level H(Q|R)=0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition. For elimination E_S: Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). ... NEVER DEFINE ZERO USING Q. Do NOT define: Zero(S) := Q(D) = Q(E_S(D)). That would build the desired bridge into the definition. Zero must use its own declared observable/op
a_rows_sample.statement: Reuses the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), calculated independently from the preservation measurement, and issues a critical prohibition against ever defining Zero in terms of Q (e.g. Zero(S):=Q(D)=Q(E_S(D))), since that would build the desired bridge directly into the definition and make the experiment circular; Zero must use its own declared observable Pi while preservation uses Q.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment must deliberately seek all four cells: Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate. ... Zero+Inadequate would directly demonstrate that Zero is not sufficient for preservation. Non-Zero+Adequate would demonstrate that Zero is not necessary for preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a four-cell crossing design (Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate) deliberately populated in all cells where possible, noting that a populated Zero+Inadequate cell would show Zero is not sufficient for preservation and a populated Non-Zero+Adequate cell would show Zero is not necessary for it, while an empty cell must be investigated for generator/contract/transformation/sample-size/mathematical-necessity/implementation causes rather than treated as a law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sweep the parameters that plausibly influence the relationship, including redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality. Every parameter sweep must be
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires declared-in-advance parameter sweeps across ten plausibly influential parameters (redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality), explicitly forbidding silent tuning to obtain balanced four-way cells.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum stratify results by: transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, elimination size |S|. Report both pooled relationship and stratified relationship. An association that disappears after stratification must NOT be reported as a general Zero-preserva
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates confounding analysis stratifying results by transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, and elimination size |S|, reporting both pooled and stratified relationships, and forbidding reporting an association as a general Zero-preservation relationship if it disappears after stratification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicitly test T x Pi ... Do not classify transformations as simply relational / element-wise and stop there. Measure the actual interaction between transformation and observable. If higher-order or preservation behavior occurs under an element-wise transformation, record it. Do not resurrect the w
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicitly testing the transformation-times-observable interaction (T x Pi) rather than stopping at a coarse relational/element-wise classification, recording higher-order or preservation behavior even under element-wise transformations, and explicitly forbidding resurrection of the already-withdrawn claim that relational transformations produce higher order while element-wise ones do not.

a_rows_sample.anchor: retain the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis. Measure k=1,2,3,...,irreducible where feasible. Do not assume higher k -> more reduction, higher k -> less preservation, irreducibility -> information loss. Those are hypotheses to test, not definitions. In particular, do not equate determination orde
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires retaining the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis (k=1,2,3,...,irreducible) in the bridge experiment while explicitly forbidding the assumptions that higher k implies more reduction, less preservation, or that irreducibility implies information loss -- these remain hypotheses to test -- and forbidding equating determination order with preservation boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retain the KR-REP-REDUCTION principle that reduction is multidimensional. Measure independently ... encoded size, cardinality, field count, representation entropy, number of relations, number of records, other declared structural measures. Do NOT invent a single 'reduction score' ... If a decoder is
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires measuring reduction multidimensionally (encoded size, cardinality, field count, entropy, relation count, record count, other declared measures) without inventing a single reduction score or assuming statistical independence among dimensions, and requires keeping representation adequacy strictly separate from decoder realization when a decoder is used, including an invertible recoding control to rule out decoder-sensitivity confounds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTROL A: A known information-preserving representation. CONTROL B: A known information-destroying representation. CONTROL C: An invertible recoding of the same representation. CONTROL D: A representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target ... CONTROL E: Positive c
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies six mandatory controls that must execute before any interpretation: A) a known information-preserving representation; B) a known information-destroying representation; C) an invertible recoding of the same representation; D) a representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target (if the generator permits); E) a positive control that the preservation test can detect information loss; F) a positive control that the Zero test can detect elimination differences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use independent TRAIN and TEST populations. Declare seeds, population size, generator, parameter distributions before execution. Persist the complete populations. No training result may influence test generation. No test result may influence transformation definitions. No post-hoc filtering may be u
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires independent train/test populations with pre-declared seeds, population size, generator, and parameter distributions, complete population persistence, and strict separation preventing training results from influencing test generation, test results from influencing transformation definitions, or post-hoc filtering to manufacture desired four-way cell counts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1: Can Zero occur while preservation fails? Q2: Can preservation hold while Zero fails? Q3: Does the Zero/Adequacy relationship survive changes in T? ... Q7: Does determination order predict preservation independently of T/Pi/C? Q8: Does the relationship survive an invertible recoding? Q9/Q10: Is a
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that the implementation explicitly answer ten falsification questions (Q1-Q10) covering whether Zero can occur without preservation and vice versa, whether the relationship survives changes in T, Pi, contract, redundancy, an invertible recoding, whether determination order predicts preservation independent of T/Pi/C, and whether any apparent relationship is explained by transformation class or by the preservation target Q itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OUTCOME A -- NO RELATIONSHIP OBSERVED ... does NOT prove universal independence. OUTCOME B -- CONDITIONAL RELATIONSHIP ... Do NOT generalize. OUTCOME C -- ROBUST RELATIONSHIP ... Only in this case may a formal bridge hypothesis be proposed for a new experiment. OUTCOME D -- DESIGN FAILURE ... Do NOT
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four mutually exclusive possible outcome classes for the experiment: A) no relationship observed (does not prove universal independence); B) conditional relationship under particular configurations (must not be generalized); C) robust relationship surviving transformations/observables/contracts/controls (the only case permitting a formal bridge hypothesis for a new experiment); D) design failure, in which case results must not be interpreted theoretically and the experiment must be revised.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md ... verify source generation, Q generation, Pi generation, transformation definitions, elimination definitions, Zero calculation, adequacy calculation, decoder calculation, train/test independence, seed handling, serialization, parameter
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies two required deliverable artifacts with exact filenames -- verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md, a 16-item forensic audit covering source/Q/Pi/transformation/elimination/Zero/adequacy/decoder generation, train/test independence, seeds, serialization, parameter sweeps, contingency tables, statistics, absence of post-hoc selection, and reproducibility; and verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-RESULTS-2026-09.md, a 22-section result document (executive verdict through epistemic status) -- with every important empirical claim required to trace to persisted data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: N_viol(R)=0 <=> H_hat(Q|R)=0, not merely N_viol=0 => H_hat(Q|R)=0 ... The asymmetry is diagnostic rather than logical.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens a stated implication into a full equivalence: for finite empirical support, N_viol(R)=0 and H_hat(Q|R)=0 are logically equivalent adequacy conditions (since zero conditional entropy forces every observed R-fiber to a single Q-value and vice versa), but the two remain diagnostically distinct -- N_viol as a structural witness locating collisions, H_hat(Q|R) as an information summary of remaining uncertainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R_{n*} is adequate, R_{n*-1} is inadequate, B_{n*}: R_{n*} -> R_{n*-1}. If adequacy is non-monotone across the chain, record that as an experimental finding rather than assuming a single boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the boundary transition B_{n*} to be defined only when both the adjacency condition (R_{n*} adequate) and its failure (R_{n*-1} inadequate) are established, distinguishing 'lowest adequate level,' 'first preservation failure,' and 'boundary transition' as three concepts that coincide only under monotone preservation behaviour across the reduction chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(R|Q)>0 => R contains variation not determined by Q ... This variation is Q-extraneous relative to the inquiry, but is not necessarily useless information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the interpretation of H(R|Q)>0 from 'R contains non-inquiry payload' to the more precise 'R contains variation not determined by Q,' explicitly noting this Q-extraneous variation may still be valuable for provenance, auditability, explainability, or answering a different future inquiry -- so H(R|Q)=0 means 'no Q-extraneous variation,' not 'nothing else is useful.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: A: Is R sufficient? <-> N_viol, H_hat(Q|R). B: Does O realize the contract? <-> A(R), F(R). C: How much Q-extraneous representation remains? <-> H_hat(R|Q). D: Where does reduction cross the boundary? <-> n*.
b_rows_sample.statement: Freezes a four-question decomposition of the KR-REP-REDUCTION protocol (sufficiency, contract realization, excess representation, boundary) each matched to a specific empirical observable (N_viol/H_hat(Q|R); A(R)/F(R); H_hat(R|Q); n*), and separates three independently-diagnosable boundary-failure kinds (Representation Boundary: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract Boundary: A(R)<1; Operator Boundary: H(Q|R)=0 but F(R)<1), noting 'information was lost != contract was violated != decoder was inadequate' as three genuinely different failure modes that a reduction can exhibit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A two-state representation can have entropy close to 1 bit, while a larger representation can have much lower entropy if its distribution is highly concentrated. ... distinguish representation capacity, storage cost, Shannon entropy, minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed requirement of strictly decreasing entropy H(R_n)<H(R_{n+1}) across the reduction chain as too strong, since entropy depends on the induced probability distribution rather than representation size; recommends requiring strictly decreasing representation CAPACITY instead, and measuring entropy, storage cost, and minimality as independent, separately reported quantities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A failed representation transition Rn -> Rn-1 demonstrates that the transformation does not preserve the contract for that sample. It does not automatically identify a unique payload S that was removed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against over-interpreting a failed reduction step: multiple eliminated components, interaction effects, transformation-induced changes, recombination, or loss of relational structure could all produce the same observed failure, so a specific eliminated set S notin Elim_{T,Pi}(D) may only be inferred when T_n has an explicit, declared elimination decomposition T_n=E_{S_n} -- otherwise report only 'T_n crosses the preservation boundary for D_i,' connecting this directly to the KR-ZERO-ORDER finding that transformation loss should not be assumed to decompose element-wise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q), therefore H(T)>=H(Q), with equality iff H(T|Q)=0 ... T(D) = G(Q(D)) almost surely ... T(D) and Q(D) are mutually deterministically recoverable almost surely.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Theorem 3's corrected attainability condition H(T(D)|Q(D))=0 and its consequence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q); corrects the proposed 'Level 4: Q-Isomorphic Representation' (from Q=O∘T alone) to 'Q-Equivalent Representation,' since factorization through T establishes only that T contains enough information to determine Q, not a bijection between the full codomains Y and Q-space; the stronger, correct claim requires both H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and H(T(D)|Q(D))=0, giving mutual a.s. recoverability T(D) <-> Q(D) rather than an unproven isomorphism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: sim_{Pi,T} = sim_Q restricted to X_{Pi,T} ... T(D) cannot literally be an element of [D]_{sim_Pi} ... D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) because Q(D)=Q(E_S(D)).
b_rows_sample.statement: Repairs two structural errors: (1) the equivalence relation sim_Pi must be defined as the global Q-induced relation sim_Q restricted to the T-dependent admissible domain X_{Pi,T}, not as an independent relation whose domain and defining condition are conflated; (2) a 'same fiber' claim mixing source-space [D]_{sim_Pi} (subset of X) with representation-space elements T(D), T(E_S(D)) (elements of Y) is type-incorrect -- the correct statement is D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) in source space, with O(T(D))=O(T(E_S(D))) as the separate representation-space consequence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_Adeq(Q) = {T: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0} ... T_Real(Pi) = {T: P(D in X_{Pi,T})=1 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D))=1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates a previously ambiguous family T_adequate(Pi) into two explicitly distinct families -- T_Adeq(Q) (transformations adequate for the inquiry alone) and T_Real(Pi) (transformations that additionally realize the whole contract, both admissibility and the fixed decoder) -- and cautions that entropy minimization T*=argmin H(T(D)) should be stated as an infimum unless existence of the minimizer is separately established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{T_n,Pi}(S_n;R^n) => Adeq(R^{n-1},Q,Pi) as the Zero-boundary hypothesis. I would not formulate it that strongly anymore ... Zero is itself a judgment produced by (D,T,Pi,S).
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed strong 'Zero-boundary hypothesis' (Zero at a reduction step implies adequacy of the next representation) as formulated too strongly, arguing instead that Zero is one observable judgment produced by the underlying tuple (D,T,Pi,S), with an unnamed interaction structure I_{T,Pi}(D,S) as the real open mathematical object -- reframing the research question from 'what does Zero predict?' to 'what structure determines the boundary at which reduction ceases to preserve the contract, of which Zero is one detection mechanism?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO discovered empirical constraints on context-dependent eliminability and revealed that relational structure may enter through the transformation/preservation pair. KR-REP-REDUCTION now independently investigates representation reduction ... using the KR-ZERO findings as controlled experimental factors and hypotheses -- not as definitions or conclusions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the relationship between the two experiment families: rather than 'KR-ZERO discovers eliminability; KR-REP-REDUCTION tests whether Zero predicts adequacy,' the corrected position is that KR-ZERO's findings become controlled experimental factors and hypotheses for KR-REP-REDUCTION, never definitions or conclusions it inherits; elevates the representation carrier (individual element vs subset vs relational structure/hypergraph/rewriting state) to a first-class unresolved research question that must be settled before R5->R2 can be properly designed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequacy != Contract Realization ... otherwise a representation could look mathematically sufficient while failing the actual preservation/operational contract.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Adequacy != Contract Realization as a hard experimental rule for KR-REP-REDUCTION, distinguishing T_Adeq(Q) (sufficient information exists) from T_Real(Pi) (the specified operator O actually realizes it, and admissibility holds), so that a mathematically sufficient representation is never conflated with one that actually satisfies the operational contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: When can source material be eliminated while preserving the contract? KR-REP-REDUCTION: How far can the representation be reduced while retaining inquiry adequacy and contract realization? The bridge is a hypothesis to test, not an established implication.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final, precise research-question separation between the two experiment families and explicitly classifies the connecting arrow (Zero_{T_n,Pi} -> candidate elimination -> R^{n-1} -> Adequacy/Realization) as a hypothesis to be tested by KR-REP-REDUCTION, never an established implication inherited from KR-ZERO; freezes a status ledger distinguishing [CORPUS] established facts, [EXP] established mathematical results (H(Q|T)=0 adequacy; H(T|Q)=0 no-excess; hence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q)), [PROP] proposed measures (Excess_Q(T)=H(T|Q); Zero predicting adequacy), and five explicit [OPEN] questions (existence of a general R5->R2 chain; the representation carrier; monotonicity; whether Zero predicts the boundary; whether relational structure in T,Pi predicts reduction difficulty).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_Q(R) = H(R|Q) as Q-relative residual representation, with excess representation as an interpretation only when the contract explicitly says those distinctions are unnecessary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the final residual-representation quantity X_Q(R)=H(R|Q) as 'Q-relative residual representation,' explicitly reserving the normatively loaded term 'excess representation' only for cases where the preservation contract itself declares the residual distinctions unnecessary, on the principle that what is unnecessary for one inquiry is not thereby unnecessary for every inquiry (provenance, uncertainty bounds, or lineage may be irrelevant to Q while still required by the broader contract Pi).

b_rows_sample.anchor: R(Q,Pi) = (D, {R_n}, {T_n}, O, Q, Pi) ... M_n = (A_n, F_n, H_hat(Q|R_n), X_Q(R_n), H_hat(R_n), N_viol,n) ... n* = min{n in {1..5} : Comp_n=1.0 and A_n=1.0 and N_viol,n=0 and H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the fully frozen KR-REP-REDUCTION experimental protocol as the object R(Q,Pi)=(D,{R_n},{T_n},O,Q,Pi) with directional chain D->T5->R5->T4->R4->T3->R3->T2->R2->T1->R1, entropy/size/count recorded independently per level (monotonicity treated as an empirical hypothesis, never assumed), a completeness-declared per-level measurement vector M_n=(A_n,F_n,H_hat(Q|R_n),X_Q(R_n),H_hat(R_n),N_viol,n), the closed-form fiber-violation formula N_viol,n=sum_r [(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2]/2, and the boundary definition n*=min{n: Comp_n=1, A_n=1, N_viol,n=0, H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}, with R_{n*} confirmed as the chain-specific preservation boundary only if the next-lower level fails at least one of those conditions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The current design does not yet fully test H-RR3 (T-Pi interaction) ... the controlled 2x2 experiment is deferred ... the next useful review is of the actual implementation and its FT-1...FT-7 execution results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes that the frozen protocol design defers the controlled 2x2 (T_extreme/realistic x Pi_extreme/realistic) test of transformation-preservation interaction (hypothesis H-RR3), so the design phase can investigate the reduction boundary and observe an association with Zero but cannot yet establish a general T-Pi interaction law; records that the theoretical/protocol design phase is complete and the next required review step is of the actual implementation's FT-1 through FT-7 execution results, i.e. an experiment run beyond the scope of this file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contract failure: NO / Operator-only failure: NO / Representation failure: YES ... A_n = 1.000 at every level ... You need a representation where H(Q|R)=0 while simultaneously O(R)!=Q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that hypothesis H-B (intending to separate representation failure, contract failure, and operator failure) found only representation failure occurring, since admissibility A_n=1.000 held at every level and the fixed decoder F=1.000 at the only adequate level R5, so no empirical state arose where Q was recoverable from R (H(Q|R)=0) yet the fixed operator O failed to recover Q (O(R)!=Q); concludes that a fixed decoder alone does not create an operator-boundary experiment -- a representation must retain enough information (H(Q|R)=0) while the chosen decoder still fails to use it -- and this chain never produced such a state, so adequacy and realization remain conceptually distinct even though this experiment did not empirically separate them along the reduction chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ascending: F_argmax = 0.8667 / descending: F_argmax = 0.3230 ... a difference of 54.37 percentage points ... yet H(Q|R2) 3.3937 vs 3.3965 is essentially unchanged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a strong empirical demonstration that representation adequacy is distinct from fixed-decoder realization: reversing a rank encoding convention (ascending vs descending) leaves Hhat(Q|R2) essentially unchanged (3.3937 vs 3.3965) and N_viol similar, yet the fixed decoder's F_argmax swings by 54.37 percentage points (0.8667 vs 0.3230); interprets this as same recoverable information under different encoding convention producing very different fixed-decoder performance, i.e. a representation can preserve the same recoverable information while a particular fixed decoder performs very differently because it interprets the representation differently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "A change carrying NO information about D..." ... The ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requests softening the phrase 'a change carrying no information about D' to the more formal 'the ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O', on the ground that what matters theoretically is not an informal claim of 'no information' but that the transformation between conventions is information-preserving/invertible; connects this directly to the project's Q-equivalence concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: bytes: 37 -> 37 -> 37 -> 25 / fields: 2 -> 2 -> 2 -> 2 / cardinality: 26826 -> 5696 -> 3288 -> 162 / entropy: 15.04 -> 12.31 -> 11.10 -> 7.17 ... there is no single obvious scalar called "amount of reduction"
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the four measured reduction-dimension trajectories (bytes, fields, cardinality, entropy) across R5..R2 and argues the evidence only establishes that no single scalar 'amount of reduction' captures all four dimensions -- i.e. reduction is multidimensional and the measured dimensions do not collapse into one common trajectory -- but four observations along a single chain cannot establish statistical independence, so hypothesis H-D's claim that 'the four dimensions move independently' should be softened to that weaker, corpus-supported statement.
