a_rows_sample.anchor: NextEpistemicAct(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,Pi) ... a_t in {Clarify, Search, Observe, ConsultResource, AssessEvidence, Determine, Defer, Act}. ... EA1..EA7
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-layer Epistemic Agency Execution Loop (front-end interaction; gap detection & classification via K_t|=Q; epistemic agency selection via a*=argmax[ExpectedGapReduction/(Cost+Risk)]; determination & output) and seven hypotheses EA1-EA7: EA1 observation!=interpretation; EA2 intent as unconfirmed hypothesis; EA3 typed gap resolution over {Semantic,Epistemic,...}; EA4 epistemic action optimization a*=argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost]; EA5 resource-bounded actions A_t=Filter(A,Resources_t); EA6 Lord/Sarathi duality (generate vs select); EA7 Determine(Evidence) before Act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t |= Q ... This notation is dangerous. ... Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) ... or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) ... should not become a new KnowledgeOS primitive. Use the existing vocabulary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the dangerous overloading of logical entailment notation K_t|=Q (which normally means semantic entailment, much stronger than intended) to the existing Adequacy/Determination vocabulary Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R), so as not to introduce a redundant new primitive, consistent with the established Determination!=Knowledge and Adequacy!=Determination!=Knowledge distinctions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t in {Semantic, Epistemic, Resource, Policy} ... I would not call these the four gap types yet ... ClassifyGap: Delta_Q -> G where G is itself still research-open.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects freezing the four-way gap taxonomy {Semantic,Epistemic,Resource,Policy} as exhaustive; recommends Delta_Q(K_t) as a typed collection of unsatisfied requirements with a ClassifyGap:Delta_Q->G mapping where G remains research-open, illustrated by four metro-scenario gap readings (inquiry gap, knowledge gap, resource gap, decision/policy gap).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap -> Opportunity -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution ... Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action. That distinction should remain intact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates four conflated concerns in the original design (what is missing, what can be done, what should be done, what is allowed) into an explicit chain Delta_t -> A_t^possible -> A_t^feasible -> a_t* -> Authorization(a_t*) -> Execute(a_t*), preserving the existing Proposal!=Decision!=Authorization!=Action distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a_t^* = argmax_{a in A_t^feasible} EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) ... KnowledgeOS should not assume that epistemic information gain is always the objective.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA4's argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost] formula as an insufficient decision rule (pure info-gain/cost could select an unsafe action, and sometimes not acting is optimal), generalizing to a_t*=argmax EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) without freezing the exact utility formula, and abstracting the capability as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,C_t,EC_t)->A_t to be determined experimentally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Resource_t(r) = (Avail,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...) ... Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) becomes meaningful.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA5's simple Filter(A,Resources_t) model to a richer per-resource state Resource_t(r)=(Availability,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...), making Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) meaningful and connecting to the existing evidence-channel work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: unless your actual observation included a specified probability model, that inequality is not established. Likewise "maintaining eye contact" was not part of the original factual description. ... Never move directly O -> P(H) without specifying the inference model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags that the worked human trace contains invented (unobserved) details treated as facts (e.g. an unstated probability inequality, 'maintaining eye contact', 'language barrier'), violating the very Observation!=Interpretation discipline KnowledgeOS is meant to enforce; recommends explicitly labeling O(observed)/I(interpretation)/H(hypothesis)/P(probability output) and never moving directly from O to P(H) without a specified inference model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q_0 -> Clarification -> Q_1 -> Clarification -> Q_2 ... until WellFormed(Q_n,C) and only then Gap(Q_n,K_t). ... Inquiry Formation ... distinct from Inquiry Resolution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the pipeline with a multi-cycle Inquiry Formation stage (Q0->Clarification->Q1->...->WellFormed(Q_n,C)) preceding gap analysis, explicitly distinguished from Inquiry Resolution; illustrated by the metro example needing a follow-up clarifying question ('Where are you going?') before the direction question is answerable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(Evidence) BEFORE Act. ... I would not make this universal. ... Required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA7 (universal Determine-before-Act) by distinguishing three action classes (epistemic actions like search/inspect/ask which may precede determination; operational actions requiring determination+authorization; safety/emergency actions taken under uncertainty), giving the conditional rule 'required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination', preserving Epistemic Decision != Operational Decision != Authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a metaphor can expose a structure without proving that the metaphor names an architectural component. ... [PROP] Lord/Sarathi is an interpretive naming lens for the two functions; not a canonical architectural name.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demotes EA6's Lord/Sarathi naming to CandidateGenerator(K_t,Delta_t,R_t)->A_t and ActionSelector(K_t,Delta_t,A_t,C_t,EC_t)->a_t, tagging Lord/Sarathi as merely [PROP] interpretive naming, invoking the prior Gita governance lesson that a metaphor can expose a structure without naming an architectural component.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract? ... A new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required capability absent from the current model, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the kernel question from 'should Epistemic Agency become a kernel operator' to 'does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract', restating the standing rule that a new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required absent capability, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation equivalence not-implies Intent equivalence ... Good action selection not-implies Correct knowledge ... Resource availability not-implies Resource reliability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a controlled factorial benchmark (fixed K_t,Q,Delta while varying resources R_t across cases A-D, then epistemic standards/risk/inquiry across cases E-G, expecting A*_A!=A*_B!=A*_C!=A*_D when resources materially differ) plus two adversarial experiments: a 'wrong assumption' test with four worlds sharing an identical observation but different underlying intent, giving Observation equivalence does not imply Intent equivalence; and a 'wrong resource' test where good action selection leads to a wrong search result, giving Good action selection does not imply Correct knowledge and Resource availability does not imply Resource reliability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a) = E[U_gap(a)] - C_resource(a) - Omega_risk(a) + U_task(a) ... the additive form is not theoretically established. ... EU = F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task) as the general specification, and treat the additive version as [PROP] EU_additive.
a_rows_sample.statement: The draft's additive four-term utility decomposition EU(a)=E[U_gap(a)]-C_resource(a)-Omega_risk(a)+U_task(a) is corrected to a general (unestablished-form) specification EU=F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task), with the additive version relegated to [PROP] EU_additive pending experimental validation, since e.g. risk may interact with epistemic benefit rather than subtract independently.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ||Delta_Q(K_t)||_G ... This is currently underdefined ... These don't naturally form a vector space. ... U_gap(a) = V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a; Q,C,EC,S) where V is a candidate gap-value/reduction function.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming a generic norm ||Delta||_G over the gap space, since typed gaps (missing value, missing dimension, contradiction, insufficient evidence, unobservable quantity, underdetermination, model insufficiency, semantic ambiguity) do not naturally form a vector space; replaces it with a general candidate gap-value/reduction function U_gap(a)=V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a;Q,C,EC,S), with an actual metric d(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}) introduced only if experiments establish a numerical structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reduction != Validation != Determination != Knowledge ... U_gap must not silently become KnowledgeGain. I recommend the term Expected Gap Resolution Value rather than Expected Epistemic Value
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues raw gap-cardinality reduction (|Delta_{t+1}|<|Delta_t|) does not imply epistemic improvement, via a worked example (3 hypotheses reduced to 1 surviving hypothesis that is false), extending Reduction!=Validation!=Determination!=Knowledge; recommends renaming 'Expected Epistemic Value' to 'Expected Gap Resolution Value' to prevent gap reduction being silently equated with knowledge gain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: rho(a) * E[DeltaRed] ... This risks double counting ... E[U(a)] = sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M) U(a,o) where reliability belongs in the observation/evidence model
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's reliability multiplier rho(a)*E[DeltaRed] as risking double-counting reliability (since it may already shape the observation distribution P(O|a,K)); recommends the cleaner E[U(a)]=sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M)U(a,o), moving resource reliability into the observation/evidence model P(O|a,R_t,...) instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Constraint != Preference. ... PrivacyViolation(a)=1 may mean a not-in A^feasible rather than EU(a)-1000. ... A^safe = {a: P(harm|a) <= epsilon} and only then a* = argmax_{a in A^safe} EU(a).
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's treatment of safety/risk as a soft utility penalty (Omega_risk subtracted, beta(R_t) scaling) to a hard feasibility constraint where appropriate: Constraint != Preference, e.g. a privacy violation should remove an action from A^feasible rather than merely penalize its utility, giving A^safe={a: P(harm|a)<=epsilon} filtered before a*=argmax_{a in A^safe}EU(a); likewise the draft's 'high-precision mode' weight adjustment is reframed as a hard safety constraint rather than a mere utility-weight change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a1) approx EU(a2) does not mean a1 equiv_sem a2. So I would call it: candidate deterministic tie-break policy not: selection invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's tie-breaking rule (favor lower latency when utilities are approximately equal) from a 'selection invariant' to a 'candidate deterministic tie-break policy', noting approximately-equal expected utility does not imply semantic equivalence of the two actions, and that the tie-break policy should itself be configurable under the active decision regime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stop or NoFurtherInvestigation ... Suppose Adeq(K_t,Q,...) = True. Continuing to investigate can have negative utility. ... This prevents KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a Stop/NoFurtherInvestigation candidate action to the action set A^possible, so that once Adeq(K_t,Q,...)=True continuing investigation can legitimately have negative utility and EU(Stop) can win, preventing KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agreement(Selection,Validation) not-implies Truth. ... ActionDecisionRecord_t containing at minimum: Inquiry, Current Knowledge State, Typed Gap, Candidate Actions, Resource States, Feasibility Results, Utility Model, Utility Parameters, Risk Policy, Selected Action, Rejected Alternatives, Decision Reason, Authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a counterfactual-action-quality experiment (estimate P(Adeq(K_{t+1}^a,Q)=1 | K_t,Q,R_t) for every candidate action and compare to the selected action, using a candidate Regret(a)=U(a*)-U(a) or outcome proxies) and an adversarial reliability test giving Agreement(Selection,Validation) does not imply Truth; requires an ActionDecisionRecord_t (inquiry, state, typed gap, candidates, resource states, feasibility, utility model/parameters, risk policy, selected action, rejected alternatives, decision reason, authorization) for inspectability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How does an epistemic system know what to do when the original request is not itself the real task? ... The inquiry was not completely known at the beginning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses a worked human example (a man asks 'Do you speak Urdu?', is answered 'How can I help?', then reveals he needs metro directions) to argue the real inquiry Q is not always known at the outset; formalizes the sequence Observation O1 -> intent hypotheses H1 -> clarifying question -> the actual inquiry Q emerging only after interaction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t |=? Q ... No. So Zero(K_t,Q) != 0 ... You have discovered an epistemic gap. But then something interesting happens. You don't simply say "I don't know." You begin an epistemic search strategy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes gap discovery (K_t does not entail Q, so Zero(K_t,Q)!=0, i.e. Delta_Q(K_t)!=empty) as triggering not a bare 'I don't know' but an active epistemic search strategy considering available resources (map, search, asking someone, information display), i.e. a policy for reducing the gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NextEpistemicAct: (K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,A,C,EC) -> a_t ... This is a major capability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'Epistemic Agency' as a missing KnowledgeOS layer answering 'how does the system decide what epistemic activity to perform next', formalized as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,Resources,Constraints,EpistemicStandard)->a_t, where a_t in {answer directly, ask clarification, search, inspect map, consult another source, compare hypotheses, gather observation, defer, report uncertainty, escalate, act}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation: Person asked "Do you speak Urdu?" Hypothesis: Person may need assistance. Confidence: uncertain ... KnowledgeOS therefore should not silently convert interpretation into fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues an interpretation (e.g. 'he needs help') that could be wrong must be tracked as a hypothesis with explicit confidence rather than silently converted into an established fact; the epistemic state should preserve observation, hypothesis, confidence, action, and how the hypothesis was later confirmed/refined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord-like function: Generate possible epistemic moves ... Sarathi-like function: Select/navigate among those possible moves.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the earlier Lord/Sarathi research not as 'Lord = God-like kernel' but as two functions: Lord(K_t,Delta,Q,Resources)->CandidateActions (generate possible epistemic moves) and Sarathi(K_t,Delta,CandidateActions,Cost,Risk,Context)->a_t (select among those moves), explicitly tagged [PROP], not to be put into Theory v1.2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic uncertainty ... Uncertainty(Intent) ... Epistemic uncertainty ... Uncertainty(Answer) ... Gap != GapType.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes semantic uncertainty (why did he ask that question -- requires clarification) from epistemic uncertainty (which direction is correct -- requires search/observation/consultation), giving Gap != GapType: the system needs to know what kind of gap it has before choosing an intervention, and notes a third possible gap where the inquiry itself is underspecified (Gap_semantic could precede Gap_epistemic).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not merely answer inquiries; it must manage the process of becoming able to answer them.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a candidate stronger definition of KnowledgeOS's purpose: the system should not merely answer inquiries but must manage the process of becoming able to answer them, extracted from seven human-behaviour-to-hypothesis mappings (interpretation separate from observation; intent as hypothesis until supported; interactive inquiry elicitation; required gap detection; gap-reduction investigation actions; epistemic action selection; determination preceding response) and recommends KR-EPISTEMIC-AGENCY-2026-09 as the next research artifact.

a_aliases: From Knowledge State to Next Epistemic Act

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'KR-EPISTEMIC-AGENCY-2026-09'

a_rows_sample.anchor: P1: Situation = KnowledgeOS state ... P3: Reiter's delta completely defines KnowledgeOS delta ... P5: Reiter resolves KnowledgeOS equality ... P9: Golog is directly usable as the KnowledgeOS workflow model ... P10: progression is sufficient for KnowledgeOS state evolution. A failed correspondence is a valuable result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Full list of ten mandatory falsification-target propositions (P1-P10) spanning situation-identity, action-event correspondence, delta-completeness, Qualify-resolution, equality-resolution, history-completeness, provenance-necessity, knowledge-operator identity, Golog-as-workflow, and progression-sufficiency, with the explicit framing that a failed correspondence is itself a valuable research result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P1: Situation = KnowledgeOS state | [TEST] | History \neq state ... P3: Reiter's delta completely defines KnowledgeOS delta | [TEST] | Missing authority, evidence ... P9: Golog is directly usable as KnowledgeOS workflow | [TEST] | Composition only
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the ten P1-P10 falsification propositions from S2538, each pre-annotated [TEST] with a one-line expected-evidence hint (e.g. P1: History!=state; P3: missing authority/evidence; P8: different semantics; P9: composition only; P10: non-monotonic issues) -- these are hints guiding the test, not yet the executed test results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is `Qualify` a **precondition**? | **REFUTED** -- `P4`. `Poss(a,s)` gates *whether an action may occur*; `Qualify` concerns *whether a qualification holds of a knowledge item*. Different type, different pipeline position | **REFUTED**
a_rows_sample.statement: Negative test P4 (Reiter solves Qualify) is applied and Qualify-as-precondition is REFUTED: Reiter's Poss(a,s) gates whether an action may occur, while Qualify concerns whether a qualification holds of a knowledge item -- a different type occupying a different pipeline position, so the correspondence fails.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity / Equality | UNRESOLVED -- cannot be placed | equiv_sem is OPEN; placing it now would decide it by implication ... Observation | UNRESOLVED | OPEN in v1.2; see 07 ... Qualification | UNRESOLVED | P4 refuted the Poss identification ... Four of six cannot be placed. Recording that is the result; guessing would be the error.
a_rows_sample.statement: Of the six candidate components tested for inside/outside placement relative to the transition mechanism, four (Identity/Equality, Observation, Qualification, plus one more per the table) remain UNRESOLVED and cannot be placed without deciding open questions (equiv_sem OPEN, Observation OPEN in v1.2, Qualification's Poss-identification already refuted by P4) by implication; recording the four as unplaced is treated as the correct result, not a gap to be guessed shut.

a_rows_sample.anchor: verdict: Situation = K_t REFUTED -- and refuted by KnowledgeOS's OWN prior evidence, not by Reiter. 9 of 10 negative tests refuted. One BOUNDED candidate (delta as an SSA), one SUPPORTED mechanism (regression), one method, one naming. NO open item closed. Theory v1.2 unchanged; no governance act.
a_rows_sample.statement: Top-line verdict of the whole Reiter/KnowledgeOS derivation programme: Situation=K_t is REFUTED, and refuted by KnowledgeOS's own prior evidence rather than by anything in Reiter; 9 of 10 negative tests (P1-P10) are refuted; the programme yields one BOUNDED candidate (delta as a successor-state-axiom shape), one SUPPORTED mechanism (regression), one CORROBORATED method, and one NEW-SYNTHESIS naming; no open item is closed, Theory v1.2 is unchanged, and no governance act was taken.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Negative tests -- 9 of 10 refuted ... None fails because Reiter is wrong. Each fails because a construct is well-defined relative to assumptions KnowledgeOS does not satisfy -- causal completeness, consistent effect axioms, factive knowledge, an existing action theory. Reiter's machinery is available exactly to the extent that KnowledgeOS supplies the assumptions it requires -- and those assumptions are precisely the programme's open items.
a_rows_sample.statement: Meta-level interpretation of the 9-of-10 negative-test refutation: no test fails because Reiter's formalism is wrong: each fails because the relevant Reiter construct is well-defined only relative to assumptions KnowledgeOS does not (yet) satisfy -- causal completeness, consistent effect axioms, factive knowledge, and an existing action theory. Reiter's machinery is therefore available exactly to the extent KnowledgeOS supplies the assumptions it requires, and those assumptions are precisely the programme's remaining open items.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reiter gives us a candidate formal foundation for delta, but he does not automatically define KnowledgeOS's delta. That distinction is critical. ... F_{t+1}=\gamma_F^+(a_t,K_t)\lor(F_t\land\neg\gamma_F^-(a_t,K_t))
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Reiter's successor-state axiom as a candidate compositional construction for delta (what an action adds, removes, and what persists because it was not removed), explicitly cautioning that this is a candidate formal foundation, not an automatic definition of KnowledgeOS's delta -- motivating the mandate to follow.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
correspondence 
eq derivation, formal analogy 
eq architectural truth, implementation usefulness 
eq canonical status ... Do NOT implement code yet. Do NOT promote any Reiter concept to a KnowledgeOS primitive, canonical architecture element, invariant, or governance rule merely because the correspondence appears intuitive.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governing nine-stage discipline (source statement -> formal interpretation -> candidate correspondence -> independent corpus test -> falsification/confirmation -> implementation usefulness -> architecture candidate -> governance -> canonicalization) with the explicit rule correspondence != derivation, formal analogy != architectural truth, implementation usefulness != canonical status; forbids code implementation or premature promotion of any Reiter concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Compare Reiter's sensing/knowledge-producing actions with the KnowledgeOS chain: W -> O -> E -> Qualify -> Assertion -> K. Investigate whether sense provides a formal analogue for observation, or whether the correspondence is invalid. ... Do not select one. The current G1 status of Qualify remains unless this research genuinely closes it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates comparing Reiter's sensing actions against the existing KnowledgeOS chain World->Observation->Evidence->Qualify->Assertion->Knowledge, testing whether 'sense' is a valid analogue for 'observation' and whether Qualify could be a precondition, action, knowledge-producing transition, epistemic test, boundary, or declared terminus -- without selecting an answer in advance; explicitly preserves the prior G1-blocked status of Qualify unless the research genuinely closes it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_1=K_2, K_1\equiv K_2, K_1\approx K_2, K_1\cong_\lambda K_2 against the Reiter distinction between situations and fluent valuations. ... Do NOT use Reiter to decide the existing normative equality question. Instead investigate whether the distinction ... reveals additional requirements for KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates an equality/identity audit using Reiter as an independent lens ONLY (not a decision-maker): compare the project's four existing equality relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ) against Reiter's situation-vs-fluent-valuation distinction, determining whether Reiter supports/contradicts/refines/is-orthogonal-to the existing (still OPEN per Steps 287-290) equality programme.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Where claims are finite or executable, write tests. Examples: successor-state consistency, persistence, conflicting effects, action precondition failure, composition, idempotence where claimed, determinism, non-determinism, regression equivalence, progression equivalence, history/state collision, observational equivalence. Do not report a mathematical claim merely because the formula looks plausible. Execute it where feasible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a mathematical audit requiring EXECUTABLE tests (not merely plausibility-checked formulas) for successor-state consistency, persistence, conflicting effects, precondition failure, composition, claimed idempotence, determinism/non-determinism, regression/progression equivalence, history/state collision, and observational equivalence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 285 Canonical state reconciliation ... 286 Philosophical-source hypothesis programme ... 287 Equality/identity/observability ... 288 Equality audit ... 289 Bootstrap/cycle audit ... 290 Equality corpus repair ... 291 Reiter/situation calculus -> formal transition model -> action/effect/persistence -> delta -> Observation/sensing -> Regression/progression -> implementation candidates
b_rows_sample.statement: Places the mandated Reiter derivation as the next numbered research step (291, later executed as step-292) in an explicit sequence following steps 285-290 (canonical state reconciliation, philosophical-source hypothesis programme, equality/identity/observability, equality audit, bootstrap/cycle audit, equality corpus repair), preferring it over continuing with another philosophical source because Reiter offers 'engineering machinery' rather than 'another conceptual analogy'; explicit caution to preserve the existing O/T, equality, and Qualify research boundaries.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HPA Supervisory Research Mandate. Date: 2026-09-02. Status: [RESEARCH] — Derivation mandate issued. Action: Execute research sequence and produce artifacts.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally issues (dated 2026-09-02, HPA Supervisory authority, status [RESEARCH]) the research mandate drafted in S2538, restructured into 15 parts matching the step-292 deliverable filenames, directing execution of the research sequence and production of the specified artifacts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 13.1 What Reiter Advances: delta -> Formal transition framework ... Boundary -> Frame problem: persistence and non-effects ... 13.2 What Remains OPEN: Qualification [OPEN] Not addressed by Reiter ... Contr [OPEN] Knowledge of contradictions, not definition ... R_req [OPEN] Not addressed
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal Gap-Update table: seven TODOs advanced by Reiter (delta, Boundary, Composition, Observation/Sensing, Regression, Progression, Operation Registry) versus seven remaining OPEN (Qualification, Equality/Identity, Provenance, Authority, Lifecycle, Contr, R_req).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 14.2 What Cannot Be Frozen: delta = Reiter's successor-state axiom | Authority/evidence missing ... Situation = Knowledge State | History \neq state ... Qualification = Precondition | Not addressed ... Observation = Sensing | Epistemic vs. physical
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal Governance Impact table distinguishing four [PROP]-status items that CAN be frozen as candidates (successor-state transition model, operation registry structure, regression-as-verification, progression-as-forward-update) from four identifications that CANNOT be frozen (delta=Reiter's-successor-state-axiom due to missing authority/evidence, Situation=KnowledgeState due to history!=state, Qualification=Precondition as not addressed, Observation=Sensing due to epistemic-vs-physical mismatch).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is `Observation` an **action**? | Reiter's sensing actions *are* actions whose effect is on knowledge -- so the shape exists. **But the corpus reopened `Observation` as `OPEN` in v1.2 and has not closed it.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Whether Observation is an action remains OPEN: Reiter's sensing actions are actions whose effect is on knowledge, so the shape exists in Reiter, but the corpus reopened Observation as OPEN in v1.2 and has not closed it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is `Observation` a **fluent**? | not decidable from either source | **OPEN**
b_rows_sample.statement: Whether Observation is a fluent is not decidable from either the Reiter source or the KnowledgeOS corpus; recorded OPEN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is sensing an action whose effect is on knowledge? | **in Reiter, yes** -- `[EXT]`. Whether KnowledgeOS's `Observation` is that kind of thing is **not** settled by Reiter's having a construct of that shape | **OPEN**
b_rows_sample.statement: In Reiter, sensing is confirmed to be an action whose effect is on knowledge ([EXT]-marked external fact). This does not settle whether KnowledgeOS's Observation is the same kind of thing -- having a construct of that shape in the source does not transfer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is `Qualify` a **precondition**? | **REFUTED** -- `P4`. `Poss(a,s)` gates *whether an action may occur*; `Qualify` concerns *whether a qualification holds of a knowledge item*. Different type, different pipeline position | **REFUTED**
b_rows_sample.statement: Negative test P4 (Reiter solves Qualify) is applied and Qualify-as-precondition is REFUTED: Reiter's Poss(a,s) gates whether an action may occur, while Qualify concerns whether a qualification holds of a knowledge item -- a different type occupying a different pipeline position, so the correspondence fails.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is `Qualify` an **operation**, or an **epistemic boundary rather than a computable function**? | **not decided.** And `KR-CONTR-EVAL` makes the third option live: the programme has already found one case where an apparent function was really a **boundary** (`reason`) | **OPEN**
b_rows_sample.statement: Whether Qualify is an operation or an epistemic boundary (rather than a computable function) is not decided; KR-CONTR-EVAL is cited as precedent making the 'boundary' option live, since that programme already found one case (reason) where an apparent function was really a boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reiter's sensing works because knowledge is modelled by an **accessibility relation** and is **factive**. `R1` decided that KnowledgeOS's object is `A_t`, an attribution, and that no component may assert `Knows`.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sensing does not transfer cleanly from Reiter to KnowledgeOS: Reiter's sensing relies on knowledge being modelled by a factive accessibility relation, but R1 decided KnowledgeOS's object is A_t (an attribution), and no KnowledgeOS component may assert Knows.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [NEG] Reiter's knowledge operator and KnowledgeOS's object are different predicates by governance decision, not by oversight. Sensing's formal guarantees are guarantees about a factive operator and do not carry over to attribution.
b_rows_sample.statement: [NEG]-tagged finding: Reiter's knowledge operator and KnowledgeOS's object are different predicates BY GOVERNANCE DECISION, not by oversight; therefore sensing's formal guarantees, which are guarantees about a factive operator, do not carry over to attribution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation   OPEN        Qualify   OPEN        O/T   OPEN ... **Reiter changes none of them.** Recorded as required by the mandate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1.1 Knowledge Status ... Values: KnownTrue, KnownFalse, Unknown, Contradictory, Underdetermined, NotAssessed. ... Evidence: Demonstrated by KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09. a_rows_sample.statement: Names Justification Mode as a P1 distinction (Evidenced/Inferred/Reported/Assumed), formalized as a tuple <phi,J,m> with a justification graph J, citing the prior 'Gap Theory v1.0' Class G3 (Lineage/Justification Gap) as its evidentiary basis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1.3 Intensional vs. Extensional Identity ... a ~ext b iff I(a)=I(b) in model M; a ~int b iff forall M, I_M(a)=I_M(b). Evidence: Essential for handling identity shifts in dynamic knowledge graphs (e.g., merging duplicate entities without losing distinct lineage). Priority: P2
a_rows_sample.statement: Names Intensional-vs-Extensional Identity as a P2 distinction, formalizing extensional equality (same value in one model M) versus intensional identity (same value across all models), motivated by merging duplicate entities in dynamic knowledge graphs without losing distinct lineage.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 2.1 Currency & Validity State ... Values: Current, Stale, Expired, Historical. ... Priority: P1 ... 2.2 Allen Interval Temporal Relations ... Before, After, Meets, MetBy, Overlaps, ... Equals. Formal Semantics: Standard Allen Algebra axioms. Priority: P2
a_rows_sample.statement: Names two temporal distinctions: Currency/Validity State (Current/Stale/Expired/Historical, P1 core invariant, to prevent stale-state propagation) and the full 13-relation Allen Interval Algebra (Before/After/Meets/MetBy/Overlaps/OverlappedBy/Starts/StartedBy/During/Contains/Finishes/FinishedBy/Equals, P2, for causality tracing and event-driven transitions).

a_rows_sample.statement: Names Evidence Directionality as a P1 distinction (Supporting/Refuting/Neutral/Dual) formalized as a signed weight function W:ExH->[-1,1], citing KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09 Scenario 4 (Conflicting Multi-Source Data) as evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4.1 Resolution Status ... Values: Resolved, Unresolved, InProgress, Irresolvable (Structural paradox). Evidence: Gap Theory v1.0 (Class G7: Unresolved Contradiction Gap). Priority: P2 ... 4.2 Boundary & Scope ... Values: InScope, OutOfScope, ConditionalScope. Priority: P2

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_req = {d_1, d_2, ..., d_k} ... K preserves a distinction d in R_req iff: for all s1,s2 in S: (s1 not~_d s2) implies (E(s1) != E(s2)). If E(s1)=E(s2) when s1 not~_d s2, the language K collapses the distinction d.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates (appearing twice, verbatim, within this file) the R_req formal specification: R_req is a set of semantic distinctions {d_1,...,d_k}, each an equivalence relation on state space S; a representation language K preserves a distinction d iff states distinguished by d are always encoded differently by E, and collapses d otherwise; a projection pi is R_req-adequate iff it preserves every distinction in R_req.

type_signature.domain: state space S with equivalence relations

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1.1 Knowledge Status ... Values: KnownTrue, KnownFalse, Unknown (Open), Contradictory (Both), Underdetermined (Insufficient information to decide), NotAssessed. Formal Semantics: Evaluated over First-Degree Entailment (FDE) double-powerset truth valuations V(phi) subseteq {T,F}. Evidence: Demonstrated by KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the R_req Knowledge Status distinction (Tier P1): six values (KnownTrue, KnownFalse, Unknown, Contradictory, Underdetermined, NotAssessed) evaluated over FDE double-powerset truth valuations V(phi) subseteq {T,F}, evidenced by KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09; notes classical logic collapses Contradictory to explosive falsity, and 3-valued logics (K3/L3) collapse Contradictory and Underdetermined into one Undefined state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 3.2 Absence of Evidence vs. Evidence of Absence ... AbsenceOfEvidence iff phi not-in K and not-phi not-in K ... EvidenceOfAbsence iff there exists e in E: e |- not-phi ... Evidence: Zero Lens Specification (Non-collapse Invariant #3).
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the Absence-of-Evidence vs Evidence-of-Absence distinction (Tier P1): AbsenceOfEvidence holds iff neither phi nor not-phi is in K; EvidenceOfAbsence holds iff some evidence e derives not-phi; cited as required by the Zero Lens Specification's Non-collapse Invariant #3, and as a distinction every other compared formalism (FOL, K3/L3, plain FDE) collapses while R_req preserves it.

type_signature.domain: K and evidence set E over proposition phi

a_rows_sample.anchor: I read the attached document in full. My assessment is that it is useful, but it is not yet safe to merge into the KnowledgeOS theory as written ... b_rows_sample.anchor: the stronger KnowledgeOS definition should be: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma) ... not: R preserves every distinction in D. The document itself notices this problem under projection adequacy, where it recommends allowing lower-tier distinctions to be lost. That observation should actually be moved up into the fundamental definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the pairwise-preservation definition of adequacy (d(x)!=d(y) implies R(x)!=R(y) for all d) to be question-relative from the start: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma), not all distinctions in D universally -- because a representation may legitimately collapse a distinction irrelevant to the current question; promotes an observation the original document made only under 'projection adequacy' up into the foundational definition.

type_signature.domain: representation R, question Q, context Gamma

b_rows_sample.anchor: For KnowledgeOS: Required != Interesting != Available in literature. A distinction belongs in R_req only if we can establish that some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement or boundary requires it. ... analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intentional/extensional, de dicto/de re ... their existence in the KR/philosophy literature does not establish that KnowledgeOS must preserve them.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the principle Required != Interesting != Available-in-literature: a distinction enters R_req only if some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement, or boundary can be shown to require it; existence in KR/philosophy literature alone (cited for analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intensional/extensional, de dicto/de re) is not sufficient grounds.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. Strong candidates: 1. Truth vs. validity ... 2. Satisfiability vs. unsatisfiability ... 3. Soundness vs. completeness ... 4. Decidability vs. undecidability ... 5. Local vs. global scope ... 6. Intensional vs. extensional ... 7. De dicto vs. de re ... B. Probably outside core R_req: Analytic vs. synthetic ... A priori vs. a posteriori ... Necessary vs. contingent ... These should remain external research candidates, not Tier 2 requirements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Splits the document's ten proposed additional distinctions into Group A (strong candidates deserving further KnowledgeOS work: truth-vs-validity, satisfiability-vs-unsatisfiability, soundness-vs-completeness, decidability-vs-undecidability, local-vs-global scope, intensional-vs-extensional, de-dicto-vs-de-re) and Group B (probably outside core R_req: analytic-vs-synthetic, a-priori-vs-a-posteriori, necessary-vs-contingent), recommending Group B remain external research candidates rather than Tier 2 requirements.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth vs. Validity -- |=alpha vs. Sigma|=alpha. This is not a clean distinction ... So the important distinction is: Validity != Entailment rather than: Truth != Validity. At the semantic level: M|=alpha is truth of alpha in a model M. Then |=alpha is validity across all models. And Sigma|=alpha is entailment from Sigma. This should be corrected before incorporating the item.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a formal error in the source document's Truth-vs-Validity distinction: the real three-way distinction is M|=alpha (truth of alpha in model M) versus |=alpha (validity: true in every model) versus Sigma|=alpha (entailment from Sigma); the document's proposed 'Truth vs Validity' pairing is not clean and should be replaced by Validity != Entailment before incorporation.

type_signature.domain: formula alpha, model M, theory Sigma

b_rows_sample.anchor: we already have a critical KnowledgeOS boundary: Satisfiability != Contr because satisfiability is relative to Semantics + Language + ModelClass. Thus: Cons_S(K) iff exists M, M |=_S K could be a candidate formal consistency property. But it must not become: Contr(K) = not Cons_S(K). ... The attached document itself later says Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status. That is actually evidence against identifying Contr with ordinary satisfiability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects identifying Contr with ordinary model-theoretic satisfiability: Satisfiability != Contr, since satisfiability is relative to Semantics+Language+ModelClass; proposes Cons_S(K) iff exists M: M|=_S K as a candidate formal consistency property distinct from Contr(K)=not-Cons_S(K), citing the source document's own admission that Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status as evidence against the satisfiability identification, and listing Contr's broader required distinctions (genuine contradiction, incompatible contexts, temporal divergence, supersession, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness).

type_signature.domain: knowledge base K under reasoning system S

b_rows_sample.anchor: soundness and completeness are properties of a reasoning system: Sound(S), Complete(S,Q). They are not properties of Knowledge itself. This should therefore be added under: Formal Representation and Reasoning rather than as a universal epistemic distinction. ... Decidability is a property of a problem/procedure/formal system ... Decidable(S,Q) ... Therefore: Decidability != EpistemicStatus. But it is extremely valuable as a reasoning-system capability/property. This fits our existing Complexity(S,Q) work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies Soundness (Sound(S)), Completeness (Complete(S,Q)), and Decidability (Decidable(S,Q)) as properties of the reasoning system S (a problem/procedure/formal-system property), not properties of Knowledge itself and not epistemic distinctions (Decidability != EpistemicStatus, distinct from Known(p) and Determined(p)); recommends filing them under 'Formal Representation and Reasoning' alongside an existing Complexity(S,Q) line of work rather than as universal epistemic distinctions in R_req.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document identifies a weakness in its own preservation criterion: it does not account for context-sensitivity. This is correct. I would make the correction stronger. Instead of D_Q we should eventually have D_Q(Gamma) ... R_req may be a global baseline, while the actual required distinction set is: R_req(Q,Gamma). This is a major improvement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the source document's own context-sensitivity self-correction: replaces D_Q with D_Q(Gamma) where Gamma bundles context, scope, time, authority, task, and representation regime; correspondingly R_req becomes a global baseline while the actually-applicable set is R_req(Q,Gamma) -- described as a major theoretical improvement over a fixed universal set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I disagree with 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' ... A Tier-1 distinction d3 could be irrelevant to that question. Then R_1 may legitimately discard d3. So Tier(d) should influence governance priority, but should not automatically determine semantic preservation. The better rule is: Requiredness(Q,Gamma) > Tier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the rule 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' as too rigid: even a Tier-1 distinction may be legitimately discarded by a representation used only for a task whose D_Q does not require it. Proposes Tier should govern governance priority, not automatically determine semantic preservation, i.e. Requiredness(Q,Gamma) takes precedence over Tier.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document says transformation invariance should preserve distinctions, but then recognizes that transformations may intentionally modify distinctions ... define a transformation's declared change set: Chg(T) subseteq R. Then: d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d. This is much better for KnowledgeOS because some operations are supposed to change state. Otherwise the preservation requirement makes state transition impossible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the transformation-invariance rule: instead of requiring T to preserve all of R_req, defines a declared change set Chg(T) subseteq R such that d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d; explicitly noting that an unconditional preservation requirement would make state transition impossible, since some operations are supposed to change state.

type_signature.domain: transformation T and distinction set R
type_signature.codomain: Chg(T) subseteq R, plus a preservation obligation on R minus Chg(T)

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document says: delta must preserve all R_req distinctions. I would explicitly reject this formulation ... What must be preserved are the invariants declared applicable to that transition. So: InvariantCustody(delta) is preferable to: PreserveAll(delta, R_req). This aligns directly with our existing invariant-custody research.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects the claim 'delta must preserve all R_req distinctions': a transition delta(K_t,a)->K_{t+1} may intentionally change status, support, currency, resolution, scope, even representation; proposes InvariantCustody(delta) -- preserving only the invariants declared applicable to that specific transition -- as preferable to PreserveAll(delta,R_req), aligned with existing invariant-custody research.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Zero requires all Tier 1 distinctions' should NOT be adopted ... Zero does not necessarily need every distinction in R_req. Instead: Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) asks what is not justified by the available representation within the declared inquiry boundary. Therefore Zero's required distinctions are: R_Zero(I,Gamma,L) not automatically all Tier-1 distinctions. This is a major correction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the claim 'Zero requires all Tier 1 distinctions': Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) does not need every R_req distinction, only R_Zero(I,Gamma,L), a distinct inquiry-relative subset; supports this by restating Zero's own existing epistemic-boundary vocabulary (Unknown!=Absent, NoEvidence!=EvidenceOfAbsence, Unresolved!=False, Representation!=Reality) as the actual grounding, rather than an automatic Tier-1 requirement.

type_signature.domain: inquiry I, context Gamma, lens L

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 'minimality' definition is not yet mathematically sufficient ... minimal relative to what? ... the empty set R=empty could trivially satisfy many formal preservation conditions. The correct direction is something like: R_req(Q,Gamma) = minimal distinctions sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria. This makes R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a mathematical gap in the source document's minimality claim (a set claimed minimal 'relative to what?' -- as stated, an empty distinction set could trivially satisfy preservation/non-collapse/compositionality conditions); corrects the definition to R_req(Q,Gamma) = the minimal distinction set sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria, making R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Completeness of R_req' is itself a dangerous concept ... There may be no useful universal set D_all. There can always be another task requiring another distinction. So instead of asking 'Is R_req complete?' we should ask: Complete relative to which task/question/domain? ... Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma) could mean: no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req. That is a tractable governance question. 'Complete for all possible knowledge representation' is not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that asking whether R_req is 'complete' in an absolute sense is a dangerous, likely-unanswerable question (no useful universal distinction set D_all can be assumed to exist, since any new task can require a new distinction); replaces it with a tractable relativized governance question Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma): no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 47 distinctions should therefore NOT be frozen as universal ... Better: 47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope. ... We should preserve KnownSet(R) without claiming R=D.
b_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the source document's claim that its 47 distinctions form a comprehensive foundation, to '47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope', distinguishing the known distinction set KnownSet(R) from a claim that R equals the (unknowable) universal distinction set D.

b_rows_sample.anchor: After filtering the document, I would extract seven concrete contributions. RQ-1 Required Distinction Set R_req(Q,Gamma) PROMOTE TO THEORY CANDIDATE ... RQ-2 Representation Preservation Preserve(R,d) PROMOTE ... RQ-3 Representation Collapse Collapse(R,d) PROMOTE ... RQ-4 Representation Adequacy Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) PROMOTE ... RQ-5 Contextual Requiredness R_req = f(Q,Gamma) PROMOTE ... RQ-6 Transformation Change Set Chg(T) subseteq R STRONG CANDIDATE ... RQ-7 Formal Reasoning Properties Sound(S), Complete(S,Q), Decidable(S,Q), Complexity(S,Q) PROMOTE AS REASONING-SYSTEM PROPERTIES
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists seven concrete contributions extracted from the filtered document, each with a promotion status: RQ-1 Required Distinction Set R_req(Q,Gamma) (PROMOTE TO THEORY CANDIDATE); RQ-2 Preserve(R,d) (PROMOTE); RQ-3 Collapse(R,d) (PROMOTE); RQ-4 Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) (PROMOTE); RQ-5 Contextual Requiredness R_req=f(Q,Gamma) (PROMOTE); RQ-6 Transformation Change Set Chg(T) subseteq R (STRONG CANDIDATE); RQ-7 Formal Reasoning Properties Sound(S)/Complete(S,Q)/Decidable(S,Q)/Complexity(S,Q) (PROMOTE AS REASONING-SYSTEM PROPERTIES).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi). Then: Loss_req = empty is a very strong adequacy condition. This is far more useful than a generic 'information loss' metric. ... FDE preserves some distinctions but collapses others. The relevant question is not 'Does FDE have four values?' It is: Does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)? Our previous experiments already showed that it does not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi) as a required-information-loss metric, with Loss_req=empty as a strong adequacy condition, judged more useful than a generic information-loss measure; reframes the earlier FDE-insufficiency finding not as 'does FDE have four values' but as 'does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)', concluding it does not (per prior experiments) -- positioning R_req as the formal language for STATING why a representation is inadequate rather than a prescription of which representation must be used.

type_signature.domain: projection pi, question Q, context Gamma
type_signature.codomain: a subset of R_req(Q,Gamma) that pi collapses

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero -> Boundary analysis -> Required distinctions rather than: Zero = absence of Tier-1 distinctions. This is a substantial theoretical improvement. ... each operation should have: Pre(delta), Post(delta), Inv(delta), Chg(delta). Then: d in Inv(delta) means the distinction must survive the transition. Whereas: d in Chg(delta) means the transition is explicitly permitted/required to change it. This is much more compatible with DDD and formal transition semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #6 — min over assurance vs. the prohibition on scalarization, both boxed in Step 211
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 Section 211.6 states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; Step 211 Section 211.17 boxes 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization.' min over a set requires a total order on the codomain, but Section 211.9 makes assurance a 6-vector (only partially ordered), so evaluating min requires exactly the scalarization Section 211.17 forbids -- the two boxed positions of one file are mutually exclusive. Aggravated by Section 211.4's ordinal-only assurance-adjacent quantities and by Section 211.17's own use of cardinal values A_s=1, A_p=0, 0.83. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #8 — F/D/P/U mandated in Step 213, applied zero times across Steps 213-215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). A machine count of applied labels in Steps 213, 214, and 215 finds 4, 0, 0 respectively, and all four occurrences in 213 are the legend itself. Zero of the hundreds of statements in the three files that mandate the labels carry one, even though Section 213.26 explicitly scopes the requirement to these reconstruction documents themselves. Severity HIGH; this is a performative contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #9 — Step 214's self-assessment table violates Step 214's own boxed evidentiary rule eight lines later
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.32 boxes 'no architectural claim should be stronger than the evidence supporting it.' Step 214 Section 214.33's final row states 'Risk of overclaiming | Explicitly controlled' -- a claim about the corpus's own overclaiming risk with zero supporting evidence, in a table that also self-awards 'Very strong' on five dimensions in a file containing no evidence at all. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #10 — Three incompatible ledger arities inside Step 214
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.1 boxes a 10-tuple EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status); Section 214.6 gives a 15-field schema table; the Section 214 tail (line 1095) gives an 8-column matrix header whose columns barely overlap the 10-tuple's. Three incompatible schemas for 'the Evidence Ledger' in one file, with no reconciliation and no statement of which is normative. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #11 — Step 215 prohibits new formulas and mints three (four) in the same file
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.30 prohibits 'creat[ing] more theoretical formulas merely because we can,' yet the same file mints R(S_i)=(O_i,L_i,A_i,V_i,U_i) (215.1), Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) (215.7), the boxed SemanticIntegrity∝DistinctionPreservation (215.10), and the boxed B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) (215.32) -- four new formal objects, none computed. Severity MEDIUM; aggravated because the proportionality is not merely new but ill-typed, and Synthesize is never specified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #12 — Step 215 exempts itself and its seven predecessors from its own discipline
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.31 (Phase 1) targets S_1...S_182 -> EvidenceLedger, goal 'understand what actually happened'; the same file's closing paragraph defers 'what we previously called Step 183 onward' to a later decision about renaming or absorption. Steps 183-215 include all eight in-scope files of this verification, so the reconstruction discipline is scoped to exclude the very documents that mandate it -- compounded by Contradiction #8 (zero labels applied). Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #13 — The scope of the derivation phase disagrees between Step 212 and Step 215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.5 states 'Steps 1-211 have largely been derivation'; Step 215 Section 215.31 and five other occurrences scope the reconstruction to S_1...S_182. The corpus states the derivation ran to 211 while scoping reconstruction to 182; the 29-step remainder is never reconciled, and 182 is never justified anywhere. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #16 — Invariants modeled as a dependency graph and as a flat conjunction, consecutively, within Step 209
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.31 states that some invariants depend on others (HistoricalTraceability depends on Identity+Versioning+Provenance), illustrated with a 24-line ASCII dependency graph. Step 209 Section 209.32 then composes all invariants as a flat, order-free conjunction I_global=AND_{i=1}^n I_i. A conjunction cannot express dependency; the two sections model the same invariant set with incompatible structures, consecutively. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.statement: States that a conversational 'step' is not necessarily an architectural contribution (some are exploratory, repetitive, corrective, editorial, etc.), so StepCount != KnowledgeCount, requiring the reconstruction to discover the actual knowledge-bearing events rather than treat all 182 steps as equal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Which architectural principles appear independently more than once? ... Convergence(I) = NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) ... We should not immediately turn this into a numerical quality score
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a convergence test: if the same architectural principle emerges from multiple unrelated observations (P_1, P_7, P_31 all pointing to invariant I), that repeated independent emergence is treated as strong evidence the principle is fundamental, formalized as Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) but explicitly not reduced to a numerical quality score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity≠State ... Knowledge≠Authority ... Unknown≠False ... CurrentState≠History ... Generation≠Validation ... Validation≠Authorization ... Claim→Evidence ... Context_A≠Context_B ... These are candidate principles, not yet declared final conclusions
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists ten candidate recurring architectural distinctions to be tested against the actual Steps-1-182 evidence rather than accepted by default (Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, Unknown!=False, CurrentState!=History, Generation!=Validation, Validation!=Authorization, Claim->Evidence, Context_A!=Context_B), explicitly labelled candidates pending evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: They are all forms of: A ≠ B where software engineering frequently makes the mistake: A ≈ B ... restoring distinctions that had been collapsed
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a deeper common structure across the recurring principles: each is an instance of A!=B guarding against a common engineering mistake of collapsing A~=B (Identity~=State, Prediction~=Truth, Knowledge~=Authority, Execution~=Outcome), proposing this pattern-of-restoring-collapsed-distinctions as possibly one of the deepest architectural themes in the entire book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving distinctions that carry semantic, temporal, epistemic or governance meaning ... SemanticIntegrity ∝ DistinctionPreservation ... a hypothesis, not a proven theorem
b_rows_sample.statement: States the 'distinction preservation' hypothesis (robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving semantically/temporally/epistemically/governance-meaningful distinctions), formalized as SemanticIntegrity proportional-to DistinctionPreservation, explicitly labelled a hypothesis to be tested against the Steps-1-182 evidence rather than a proven theorem; connects this across DDD (Entity!=ValueObject), mathematics (x!=y), statistics (Observed!=Inferred, Correlation!=Causation), governance (Capability!=Authority) and AI engineering (Generation!=Verification) as convergent instances of one meta-principle: do not collapse distinctions that matter.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Krishna ~ Perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations ... What would a software system need if it were required to preserve continuity across changing states? ... Versioning, Provenance, History, Lineage, Context
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a careful literary (not architectural) interpretation of Krishna as 'a perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations', translating this into the engineering question of what a system needs to preserve continuity across changing states (versioning, provenance, history, lineage, context), explicitly warning against the trivializing claim 'Krishna is the system's memory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Philosophical Analogy ≠ Technical Proof ... Outcome A ... retrospective analogy ... Outcome B ... repeatedly influenced ... Outcome C ... independently emerged technically and philosophically ... the most interesting result
b_rows_sample.statement: States three possible historical outcomes for the Gita lens's actual role to be determined by the reconstruction rather than assumed: (A) it was purely a retrospective analogy applied after the fact, (B) it repeatedly and genuinely influenced engineering questions during development, (C) the same principles independently emerged both technically and philosophically -- rated the most interesting possible result, expressible as EngineeringObservation<->PhilosophicalReflection without either proving the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a technical invariant existed before the corresponding Gītā reflection ... TechnicalDiscovery -> PhilosophicalRecognition ... those are different histories. The Evidence Ledger will tell us which actually occurred
b_rows_sample.statement: States that chronology determines which of two different intellectual histories occurred (technical discovery preceding philosophical recognition, or vice versa) and that only the actual Evidence Ledger -- not narrative preference -- can establish which; reframes Step 215's most important task as determining 'when did the idea enter the reasoning', not merely what was concluded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 182 Steps -> 43 SignificantEvents -> 17 CoreInsights -> 8 ArchitecturalPrinciples -> 4 MajorThemes. The exact numbers are unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a compression pipeline reducing 182 raw steps to a small number of significant events, core insights, architectural principles, and major themes (illustrative counts only, explicitly not fixed), arguing the book should present the intellectual structure hidden inside the steps rather than the 182 steps themselves; proposes an intermediate 5-epoch structure (Problem Recognition -> Experimentation -> DDD/Domain Modeling -> Mathematical/Epistemic Formalization -> KnowledgeOS/AI-Engineering Architecture) explicitly not to be frozen before the evidence determines it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture_observed ... Architecture_designed ... Architecture_implemented ... Architecture_proposed ... Observed ≠ Intended ≠ Implemented ≠ Target
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that the single word 'architecture' conflates at least four distinct referents (observed, intended, implemented, target/proposed) that may differ from each other, proposing Observed!=Intended!=Implemented!=Target as a central reconstruction rule; separately notes that linguistic markers in generated text ('should' signals P, 'the code contains' signals F if verified, 'therefore requires' signals D) can help automatically classify epistemic status at scale.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step Source Artifact Date/Sequence Primary Topic Type Observation Fact Hypothesis Experiment Result Derived Insight Decision Rejected Alternative Architectural Principle Invariant Evidence Gita Connection Status [F/D/P/U] Confidence Open Question
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the Step 215 Artifact: a 19-column Master Reconstruction Matrix schema intended as the master source for eventual book-writing, including a dedicated 'Gita Connection' column and 'Rejected Alternative' column.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not: rewrite the book; freeze the chapter structure; invent missing evidence; merge competing concepts; eliminate contradictions; assume implementation ... Reconstruct. Analyze. Synthesize. Write.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists nine things not to do before reconstruction is complete (rewrite the book, freeze chapter structure, invent missing evidence, merge competing concepts, eliminate contradictions, assume implementation, over-architect philosophical analogies, assign arbitrary percentages, create formulas for their own sake), sequencing the correct order as Reconstruct -> Analyze -> Synthesize -> Write.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1 — Archaeology ... Phase 2 — Separation of Concerns ... Phase 3 — Synthesis ... This is the correct point at which Claude should eventually begin chapter-by-chapter writing. Not before
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-phase book-production architecture: Phase 1 Archaeology (S1..S182 -> Evidence Ledger, understand what happened), Phase 2 Separation of Concerns (separate Facts from Derivations from Proposals from PhilosophicalInterpretations, preventing conceptual contamination), Phase 3 Synthesis (Evidence->Patterns->Principles->Architecture->Book), stating chapter-by-chapter writing is correct only after all three phases, not before.

b_rows_sample.anchor: B = Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) ... ClaimStrength ≤ EvidenceStrength ... PhilosophicalReflection ≠ TechnicalEvidence ... CurrentArchitecture ≠ TargetArchitecture
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final synthesis equation for the whole book-generation process, B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection), subject to three boxed constraints (ClaimStrength<=EvidenceStrength, PhilosophicalReflection!=TechnicalEvidence, CurrentArchitecture!=TargetArchitecture), explicitly framed as protecting the book against retrospective rewriting, overclaiming, and confusing philosophy with engineering proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: IT SPECIFIES A METHOD. It reconstructs nothing.
